na13cbf974280: by Majed M. Aljabri, Bandar S. Alharbi, Endale Alemayehu Ali Background Psychological stress is highly prevalent among nursing students. The clinical exposure is a major factor contributing to psychological stress, but there is a lack of consistent evidence, particularly in the context of Middle Eastern countries. The aim of this study was to quantify the association between clinical exposure and perceived stress among nursing students, and to assess whether perceived social support moderates this relationship. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study among nursing students from King Saud University. The Perceived Stress Scale was used to measure psychological stress, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support was employed to measure perceived social support. The clinical exposure was quantified as the average number of hours spent per week. We employed multivariable linear regression to determine the association. The regression analysis was adjusted for age, gender, living arrangements, and employment status. Results Higher perceived social support was significantly associated with lower perceived stress (β = −0.05, 95% CI −0.09 to −0.01). Clinical exposure was not significantly associated with perceived stress. Students living alone had significantly lower levels of perceived stress (β = −0.37, 95% CI −0.63 to −0.11), as did students working part-time (β = −0.34, 95% CI −0.54 to −0.13). The interaction model revealed that perceived social support was inversely associated with perceived stress levels (β = −0.14, 95% CI −0.23 to −0.04). A statistically significant interaction was observed among students with less than 10 hours of clinical exposure per week. This exploratory finding suggests that the association between perceived social support and stress may differ among students with limited clinical exposure. However, the finding was based on a single statistically significant interaction and should be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating. Conclusions Higher perceived social support was associated with lower levels of perceived stress among nursing students. Interventions aimed at enhancing the social support system may be beneficial in reducing stress, especially during the early clinical exposure period.
n4057f27a2586: An 18-month prospective, non-randomized comparative observational study evaluated the effects of different optical corrections on myopia progression, binocular vision, and visual performance in Spanish children. Forty-five myopic participants aged 9–14 years were allocated to single-vision lenses (SV), low-addition progressive addition lenses (PALs), or defocus-incorporated multiple segments lenses (DIMS). Assessments included spherical equivalent (SE) and axial length (AL), comprehensive accommodative function evaluated by measuring amplitude of accommodation, positive and negative relative accommodation, accommodative facility, and accommodative response, and binocular function evaluated by measuring phorias, fusional vergences, and stereopsis. In addition, contrast sensitivity (CS), visual disturbance index (VDI), and subjective visual quality were assessed at baseline and at 6, 12, and 18 months. After 18 months, SE progression was −0.59 D for SV, −0.51 D for PALs, and −0.30 D for DIMS, corresponding to a 49% reduction with DIMS compared to SV. AL increased by 0.24, 0.27, and 0.23 millimeters, respectively, although inter-group differences were not significant for AL. Accommodative and binocular functions, visual acuity, CS, and VDI remained stable, while distance stereopsis improved in the DIMS group. These findings suggest an association between DIMS lens wear and reduced myopia progression compared with SV lenses in this cohort, without clinically relevant differences in accommodative or binocular function, visual acuity, or subjective visual quality.
na764a08806e4: Early social experience is critical for the maturation of social behavior, and its disruption during juvenile development may confer long-term psychiatric vulnerability. Juvenile social isolation (j-SI) after weaning is widely used as a model of early social deprivation; however, its developmental and sex-specific effects on spontaneous social interaction remain unclear. We examined the behavioral consequences of post-weaning social isolation in male and female C57BL/6J mice (Mus musculus). Mice were individually housed from postnatal day (P)21, and spontaneous social interaction was assessed longitudinally at P35, P49, and P63 during prolonged cage-based sessions using an augmented reality-based behavioral monitoring system. Locomotor activity, inter-mouse distance, mean contact duration per initiated encounter, and interaction dynamics were quantified during the light and dark phases. Juvenile social isolation was associated with greater inter-mouse distance across most developmental stages and sex-phase combinations, whereas reductions in mean contact duration per initiated encounter varied by sex, developmental stage, and light/dark phase. Locomotor activity varied by developmental stage and sex, with late-emerging increases particularly evident during the dark phase in isolated mice. In contrast, lower interaction-partner switching in isolated males was detected only at the earliest stage (P35) during the light phase. An important design feature is that isolated mice were reunited at testing with cage mates from which they had been separated for more than two weeks and were therefore effectively unfamiliar, whereas group-housed mice were tested with continuously familiar cage mates; the reported effects therefore reflect social isolation together with its intrinsic reduction in social familiarity. These findings indicate that continued post-weaning social isolation is associated with persistent, sex-specific alterations in sociability and social interaction dynamics. Our results further suggest that juvenile social experience may shape the developmental maturation and temporal organization of social interaction across adolescence and early adulthood.

nb749d681d209: Background We aimed to establish thresholds for assessing clinically meaningful pain improvement after spinal injections using numerical rating scale (NRS) and patient-reported relative reduction (PRR) of pain. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 1,828 patients who received spinal injections at our spinal intervention center and completed a 2-week follow-up telephone interview in 2017. NRS absolute and relative reductions were calculated using the NRS scores before injection and at follow-up. The PRR and 5-point global perceived effect (GPE; 1, completely recovered; 2, much improved; 3, slightly improved; 4, no change; and 5, worsened) were recorded. The mean ± standard deviation (SD) of NRS absolute reduction, NRS relative reduction, and PRR in the GPE 2 and 3 subgroups were calculated. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis was used to determine the cutoffs for NRS absolute and relative reduction and PRR in predicting the substantial clinically important difference (SCID, GPE 1–2) and minimal clinically important difference (MCID, GPE 1–3). Results The mean ± SD of NRS absolute and relative reduction, and PRR in the GPE 2 and GPE 3 were 4.5 ± 1.8, 65.4% ± 21.1%, and 67.7% ± 14.8% and 2.4 ± 1.4, 36.8% ± 22.5%, and 35.7% ± 16.1%, respectively. The cutoffs for predicting SCID and MCID were NRS absolute reduction of ≥3 and ≥1, NRS relative reduction of ≥50% and ≥10%, and PRR of ≥50% and ≥20%, respectively. Conclusions The NRS absolute and relative reduction and PRR thresholds were established to differentiate SCID and MCID in terms of pain improvement after spinal injections.
nce85b72d36b3: One important purpose of back support exoskeletons (BSEs) is to reduce the stress to the lumbar spine and alleviate the low back pain. However, most previous studies introducing BSEs have argued for their effectiveness based only on easily measurable physiological outcomes such as muscle activation. Motivated by this gap, we examined whether the muscle activation of the back muscle during load handling with a passive BSE can faithfully reflect the estimated L5–S1 joint reaction forces and subjective perceptions. Experiments involving 12 healthy young adults revealed that the BSE significantly reduced average thoracic erector spinae muscle activation during both lifting and lowering the load, and lumbar erector spinae muscle activation during lowering. The BSE also reduced integrated thoracic erector spinae muscle activation during lowering. L5–S1 joint reaction forces were also significantly reduced by the BSE (p < 0.001). Participants reported a lower rate of perceived exertion (p < 0.05). However, the lack of associations among all metrics suggests that inferring one measure from another remains limited when evaluating the efficacy of a BSE.
n8b7ca2b56e24: Generative AI tools are now routinely used by Chinese Language and Literature majors for tasks once considered the province of individual literary craft: drafting verse, shaping narrative prose, revising fiction. Two competing accounts describe what this means for students’ confidence in their own creative writing. A cognitive-offloading account holds that repeated reliance on AI displaces the mastery experiences through which writing self-efficacy is built, so reliance erodes confidence over time. A compensatory-use account holds the reverse: students whose confidence is already low turn to AI to avoid the discomfort of unassisted composition, so low confidence drives reliance. Cross-sectional and standard cross-lagged designs cannot separate these accounts because they confound stable between-person differences with genuine within-person change. We addressed this using a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) across four waves spanning one academic year among Chinese Language and Literature undergraduates (N = 390 recruited; N = 387 analyzed under full-information maximum likelihood, of whom 298 supplied complete four-wave data). Generative AI writing reliance (GAWR) and literary creative writing self-efficacy (LCWSE) were assessed at each wave. The trait-level association between the two constructs was negative and could not be distinguished from zero (r = −.342, Δχ²(1) = 2.26, p = .133). At the within-person level, declines in self-efficacy predicted subsequent increases in reliance (β = −.276, p p = .072). We state explicitly that this second result is not interpretable as evidence against erosion: a Monte Carlo power analysis put this design's power to detect an effect of that magnitude at 53.2%, close to a coin flip, so the erosion pathway is undetermined in these data and this null supplies no basis for concluding that erosion does not operate. A direct comparison of the two cross-lagged paths favored compensation (Δχ²(1) = 8.83, p = .003; bootstrap 95% CI for the difference [.020, .218] across 5,000 resamples), with the qualification that this comparison sets an adequately powered estimate against an underpowered one and therefore describes what this design was able to detect. Compensation is the pathway this study establishes; whether reliance also erodes confidence over a longer horizon is an open question. We discuss implications for writing pedagogy in Chinese Language and Literature programs and for how underpowered null results should be interpreted in AI-in-education panel research.
n9fc858c7ac10: Pigeons and quail contribute to poultry production, nutrition, and livelihoods in Bangladesh; however, their role in avian influenza virus (AIV) circulation remains poorly understood. These poultry species are widely reared and traded alongside chickens and ducks in household farms, commercial systems, and live bird markets, where inadequate biosecurity may create an overlooked ecological niche for AIV circulation, reassortment, and potential zoonotic spillover. Between November 2021 and April 2022, we conducted a cross-sectional study in Chattogram, Bangladesh, to estimate the prevalence and subtype-specific distribution of AIV and to identify factors associated with AIV positivity in pigeons and quail. A total of 300 birds (108 pigeons and 192 quail) were sampled from households, commercial farms, and live bird markets. Oropharyngeal and cloacal swabs were collected from each bird and tested for the AIV matrix gene using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, followed by subtype-specific detection of H5, H7, and H9. Data collected from bird owners and traders included bird demographic characteristics, bird source, and health status using a structured questionnaire. The overall prevalence of AIV was 14.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 10.6–18.8). Quail had a higher prevalence (18.2%, 95% CI: 13.0–24.4) than pigeons (7.4%, 95% CI: 3.3–14.1). Among detected subtypes, H9 was most prevalent (11.3%, 95% CI: 7.9–15.4), followed by hemagglutinin (HA)-untyped (2.7%, 95% CI: 1.2–5.1) and H5 (0.3%, 95% CI: 0.001–1.8), while H7 was not detected. Quail had higher odds of AIV positivity than pigeons (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 4.1, 95% CI: 1.8–10.6); clinically sick birds (aOR = 2.9, 95% CI: 1.4–6.2) and birds sampled from household farms (aOR = 2.8, 95% CI: 1.2–6.5) also had higher odds of AIV positivity. These findings indicate that pigeons and quails, which are understudied poultry species, may contribute to the maintenance and transmission of AIV within mixed poultry production and marketing systems in Bangladesh. Integrating these species into routine AIV surveillance is therefore necessary to strengthen early detection, inform control strategies, and reduce the risk of zoonotic spillover.
nc9e1be4c988e: Currently, there are still no reliable pre-treatment biomarkers for vedolizumab in ulcerative colitis. To investigate baseline mucosal signals, we reconstructed the discovery cohort from GSE73661 and evaluated the derived panel in the blood samples from GSE191328 and the independent mucosal RNA-seq cohorts from E-MTAB-7845. The reconstructed cohort comprised 24 baseline samples, including 14 composite responders and 10 non-responders. Through repeated LASSO variable selection, the study identified an exploratory gene set consisting of ZNF689, TPRXL, ZC3H10, and MRPL55. The selection procedure yielded a mean held-out AUC of 0.611 across 18 complete nested-validation repetitions; this does not independently validate the final gene set. When the fixed gene set was projected exploratorily, the AUC for 17 blood samples was 0.458 (95% CI 0.162–0.755), and the AUC for 27 independent UC mucosal samples was 0.534 (95% CI 0.293–0.775). The apparent AUC of this gene set on the discovery set was 1.000, and 500 full-process bootstrap analyses indicated that gene selection was unstable. Among the three targeted inflammatory panels, interferon-γ showed a directional difference that was not statistically significant (mean GSVA score difference −0.425; nominal P = 0.066; adjusted P = 0.197). Expression scales and clinical endpoints differed across cohorts. The above results describe post-selection separation within the discovery cohort and do not establish reproducible predictive performance, tissue specificity, or a definitive four-gene signature.
n234e524385f5: This longitudinal study examines how preschool children’s phonological awareness and emergent literacy skills relate to their early writing performance in first grade. Conducted within the context of a transparent Turkish orthography, the study aims to identify early cognitive-linguistic correlates of subsequent writing development. A total of 97 children (aged 66–77 months) from preschools in a socioeconomically diverse Turkish district were followed over two academic years. In the first year, participants were assessed using the LAP-3 Early Literacy Subtest and the Phonological Awareness Test to measure their emergent literacy and phonological skills. One year later, their writing performance was evaluated using a validated sentence construction assessment. Non-parametric statistical tests and correlation analyses were conducted to examine developmental variations and relationships among the variables. Results revealed statistically significant correlations between early writing performance and both phonological awareness (r = .46, p < .01) and emergent literacy (r = .32, p < .01). Specific sub-skills such as syllable segmentation, rhyming awareness, and letter-sound correspondence showed the strongest associations with writing performance. These skills did not differ significantly by age or gender. The findings highlight the foundational role of preschool phonological and emergent literacy skills in early writing development. This study contributes empirical data from a transparent orthography. Given the correlational design, these findings should be interpreted as evidence consistent with developmental literacy theories rather than as confirmation of causal or predictive mechanisms; they emphasize the importance of early identification and instructional support in preschool settings to promote future writing success.
n07771aa7b087: The democratization of sequencing has led to a wealth of high-quality genome assemblies from across the Tree of Life. One pattern that has emerged is that chromosomes within a genome can vary drastically in their gene density (e.g., human chromosomes 13 and 19, with gene densities of 17.5 and 60.5 genes per megabase, respectively). To our knowledge, the cause of this variation in gene density has not been explored. In this study, we leveraged genome assemblies of 262 vertebrate species to examine the range of within-genome variation in gene density. We combined gene density data with repeat landscape analyses in each species. We predicted that genomes with more recently expanded repeat families should show greater variation in gene density, because repetitive elements accumulate unevenly across the genome, while chromosomal rearrangements such as fusions, fissions, insertions, deletions, and inversions homogenize gene density over time. Our empirical analysis reveals a significant yet variable effect of repeat expansions, with additional processes likely contributing to variation in gene density.
n91013429db19: by Henry T. Phan, Chun-Wei Lin, Brittany L. Stinger, Joseph B. DeGrandchamp, L. J. Nugent Lew, Serena J. Huang, Jay T. Groves Upon ligand binding, the kinase domain of EGFR phosphorylates multiple tyrosine residues on the receptor cytoplasmic tail through a trans-autophosphorylation process. Phosphotyrosine sites on activated receptors recruit Grb2, which further recruits SOS to initiate downstream signaling by activating Ras. Multivalent binding between SOS and Grb2, as well as direct Grb2:Grb2 interactions, contribute to formation of a protein condensate of activated EGFR. The condensed state of EGFR facilitates autoinhibition release in SOS and exerts regulatory control over signal propagation from activated EGFR to Ras. While kinase activity of EGFR is an essential driver of this signaling process, phosphorylation at residue Y160 on Grb2 blocks Grb2:Grb2 binding and can interfere with EGFR condensation. Here, using a reconstituted system, we examine how titrating kinase activity in the EGFR system can both promote and inhibit signal output to Ras. The results reveal how effects of tyrosine kinase inhibition can, under some circumstances, promote Ras activation by inhibiting negative feedback through Grb2 phosphorylation and disruption of a Grb2 SH2/SH3 dimer interface.
nc4c4886abe5e: Arterial cannulation for cardiopulmonary bypass in small dogs is challenging because small vessel diameters may preclude use of appropriately sized pediatric arterial cannulas. Although off-label use of 14-gauge hemodialysis catheters has been reported, their pressure–flow characteristics under small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass conditions remain unclear. This in vitro study evaluated one 8-French pediatric arterial cannula and six 14-gauge hemodialysis catheter specimens—separate side-hole and sealed specimens at effective lengths of 25, 32, and 38 mm—in a closed-loop mock circuit for a 3-kg small dog. A 34% (w/w) glycerol–water solution (viscosity 2.8 cP at 28°C) served as an approximate Newtonian blood analogue. The Stockert S5 pump flow-rate setting was increased from 50 to 350 mL/min; 50–300 mL/min was prespecified as the primary analysis range and 350 mL/min as exploratory. The reported outlet pressure was recorded 1,000 mm upstream of the test device, while inlet pressure was monitored 300 mm downstream and regulated to 60 mmHg; six technical runs per condition were conducted using the same physical device and circuit setup. Within the primary analysis range, outlet pressure was approximately 136–137 mmHg at 300 mL/min; mean differences for the 14-G specimens versus the 8-French cannula were +0.33 to +0.67 mmHg, with 95% confidence intervals from −1.33 to +2.15 mmHg. At 350 mL/min, outlet pressures were higher for all three side-hole 14-gauge specimens than for the 8-French cannula. At 300 mL/min, outlet pressure was approximately 2–3 mmHg lower for the side-hole specimens than for the sealed specimens across all catheter lengths. Together, these findings indicate small observed circuit-level differences in outlet pressure among tested devices within this standardized mock small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit, but do not establish formal equivalence, device-to-device interchangeability, or clinical validity.
n06cee474f624: This study examined the influence of older age and race (White/Black/Arab) on stereotypes of women. To evaluate whether age and race shape stereotype content for an intersectional group relative to its superordinate racial or superordinate older age identities, 525 Amazon Mechanical Turk participants were asked to list up to five words or short phrases that most people associated with these target groups. Overall, the study found stronger support for a distinctiveness hypothesis, whereby the most distinct identity of an individual’s intersectional identity influenced their associated characteristics. For example, because being White is common in the United States, old White women had more stereotypes in common with their old superordinate identity than their White identity. This suggests that the nation’s population characteristics may be predictive of the stereotypes associated with different intersectional groups. Overall, this research reveals the complex interplay between stereotypes of age and race for women, underscoring the need to acknowledge intersectional identities and cultural norms. Such insights can enhance our pursuit of inclusive and accurate societal perceptions.
naadd5d187088: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) is an early mediator of ischemia–reperfusion injury (IRI), however, the evidence on its role in orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT), particularly with donation after circulatory death (DCD) grafts is limited. Given its key regulatory function, this study investigated the effects of IRI on graft injury and assessed whether the use of ISO-1, a small-molecule MIF-inhibitor, affect IRI in a rat DCD-OLT model. 196 male Lewis rats were randomized into DBD control, DCD-30 min, DCD-60 min, DCD-30 + ISO-1, and DCD-30 + vehicle groups (n = 7/group/time-point). ISO-1 was administered before controlled cardiac arrest (0–60 min) and 3 h cold preservation before arterialized OLT. Animals were sacrificed at 1, 3, 24, and 168 h post-reperfusion. DCD grafts showed marked injury, with the DCD-60 group exhibiting lethal IRI. ISO-1 significantly reduced early hepatocellular injury compared with vehicle (AST:294 ± 63 vs 867 ± 211 IU/L, p = 0.017) and resulted in values comparable to DBD controls. Serum HMGB-1 (11 ± 2.8 vs 26 ± 6.2 pg/mL, p = 0.045) and MIF (45 ± 5.3 vs 144 ± 27.5 ng/mL, p = 0.034) levels were similarly decreased following ISO-1 application. ISO-1 improved graft microcirculation at 24 h, attenuated histological injury, and was associated with an altered time course of CD163 + macrophage infiltration. ISO-1 pre-treatment attenuated hepatocellular injury and was associated with improved graft microcirculation and reduced DAMP release, supporting further mechanistic and translational evaluation in DCD liver transplantation.
n5d712a03efcb: In response to the accuracy loss caused by lightweight networks on edge devices and the difficulty in accurately detecting small defect targets, this paper studies the lightweight You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) transmission line insulator defect detection algorithm based on Three-Branch Attention Mechanism (TBAM) and Enhanced Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network (EMSFFN), which can perform high-precision detection on edge intelligent devices of unmanned aerial vehicles. Aiming at the problem of significant differences in the number of image categories in the current aerial insulator defect dataset, the dataset was expanded through image data augmentation to generate more minority class samples, balance the number of samples in each category. Experiments show that compared with YOLOv7, YOLOv8, YOLOv9, Detection Transformer (DETR) and Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN), the model parameters and computational complexity of TBAM-YOLOv8-EMSFFN are relatively low. Its AP reaches 99.2% and the mAP reaches 98.7%. Therefore, the TBAM-YOLOv8-EMSFFN model is suitable for unmanned aerial vehicles carrying edge intelligent devices to achieve power inspection.
n362e09c67089: by Veronica A. Pear, Christopher E. Knoepke, Lisa B. Geller, Amy Barnhorst, Ari Davis, Rose Kim, Garen J. Wintemute Background Extreme risk protection orders (ERPOs) temporarily prohibit the purchase and possession of firearms by people at high risk of harming themselves or others. This study drew on the experiences of ERPO respondents to learn about the perceived short- and long-term consequences of the law. Methods For this qualitative descriptive study, we conducted 24 semi-structured interviews between March and November 2024 with respondents to ERPOs issued in California between 2016 and 2020. We purposively sampled 250 respondents for whom we had previously abstracted ERPO court case data to ensure adequate representation across domains of interest (e.g., demographics, location) and invited respondents to participate in the study by mail. All interviews were recorded, double coded, and thematically analyzed. Results Our diverse participants described heterogeneous consequences across 4 domains: violence risk, legal/economic outcomes, opinions/attitudes, and social/emotional wellbeing. Two participants believed their ERPOs prevented violence and 1 was unsure; the rest believed that they would not have committed violence irrespective of the ERPO. Some perceived the ERPO to have had negligible effects on their lives, while others described both positive consequences, including self-reflection and behavior change, and negative consequences, including employment or housing difficulties, stigmatization, damaged relationships, loss of trust in legal institutions, and perceived exacerbation of violence risk. Participants reported that they were not connected to mental health care or other supportive services through the ERPO process. Conclusions Participants perceived ERPOs to have varied and mixed consequences. These accounts identify outcomes that warrant consideration in ERPO research, policy, and implementation. Future research should assess the prevalence and distribution of these consequences and evaluate whether policy refinements can reduce adverse experiences without compromising the public health benefits of these laws.
n7ecd762c701c: This retrospective study examined the historical progression of Olympic swimming performance across 24 Olympic Games from Paris 1924 to Paris 2024. Finalist race data for 1553 women and 1641 men were extracted from the official World Aquatics database, including final times, reaction times, and calculated swimming speeds across all strokes (freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly) and Olympic distances (50–1500 m). Across all strokes and distances, final times demonstrated substantial reductions over the century, with the most pronounced improvements observed in freestyle and long-distance events. The largest percentage improvements in performance were observed during specific Olympic cycles, including 1956, 1972, and 2008, which coincided with major developments in pool engineering, competition regulations, training methodologies, and swimsuit technology. Swimming speeds increased consistently in all events, while reaction-time analyses revealed significant improvements across Olympic Games during the period in which reaction-time data were recorded. Overall, these findings demonstrate substantial long-term improvements in Olympic swimming performance and provide a comprehensive historical overview of performance changes across strokes, distances, and sexes. The periods associated with the largest performance improvements coincided with major technological, biomechanical, and regulatory developments in the sport. The results may serve as valuable benchmarks for coaches, athletes, and sports scientists to evaluate long-term performance trends and prepare for future international competitions.
n9276a1f673a9: Candida auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen and a major global health threat, highlighting the urgent need for new therapeutics. We screened ~2,600 FDA-approved drugs and clinical compounds and identified darapladib (DAL), a phospholipase A2 inhibitor, as a potent antifungal agent against multidrug-resistant C. auris. DAL exhibited antifungal activity against all tested C. auris isolates and showed broad-spectrum activity against other tested clinically important fungal pathogens, including other Candida, Cryptococcus, and mucormycosis-associated species, with minimum inhibitory concentrations of 4–16 μg/mL. DAL also displayed rapid fungicidal activity against C. auris and synergized with amphotericin B against C. auris and filamentous fungal pathogens. More importantly, serial exposure of C. auris to subinhibitory concentrations of DAL for 16 passages did not result in detectable resistance. Mechanistic studies indicated that DAL acts through an ergosterol-dependent membrane targeting mechanism, as exogenous ergosterol attenuated its activity and ergosterol-related haploinsufficient mutants showed reduced susceptibility. Consistent with this mechanism, DAL increased membrane permeability, nucleic acid leakage, and reactive oxygen species. In a Caenorhabditis elegans–C. auris infection model, DAL reduced the C. auris burden to below the limit of detection. Together, these findings support further investigation of DAL as a repurposed antifungal candidate against drug-resistant fungal infections.
ne863189ac21e: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a respiratory disease with a high degree of cellular heterogeneity and molecular complexity, characterized pathologically by persistent airflow limitation and an inflammatory-tissue remodeling cascade involving multiple cell types. Traditional transcriptomics lack the resolution to precisely define cell subpopulation roles in COPD. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) overcomes this limitation by enabling high-resolution analysis of cell-type-specific mechanisms in COPD. A total of 101,009 cells from three scRNA-seq datasets were integrated to profile COPD-related molecular features and cell interactions at single-cell resolution. Analysis identified four major cell types and 17 distinct cell subtypes. Cell–cell communication analysis revealed a significant reduction in signaling activity of macrophages and fibroblasts, whereas certain immune cells exhibited enhanced signaling, suggesting that immune dysregulation plays a pivotal role in COPD pathogenesis. Further analysis focused on macrophage-dominant myeloid cells and fibroblasts, uncovering their critical roles in inflammation modulation and fibrosis progression. Meanwhile, this study also identified 19 chemicals that may influence COPD progression by modulating cellular gene expression. This study provides an important molecular basis for unraveling the cell-cell interaction network of COPD and elucidating the mechanism of each cell subpopulation in the disease process.
na079da84ba3d: Background Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health challenge, with rapidly rising incidence in low- and middle-income countries, including Ethiopia. Survival outcomes are compromised by late-stage presentation, limited therapeutic capacity, and weak post-treatment follow-up. Although survival analysis is critical for characterizing CRC prognosis, insufficient attention has been given to the performance and validity of commonly applied survival models in Ethiopian populations, particularly when statistical assumptions are violated. Objective To identify key clinical and treatment-related prognostic factors influencing overall survival among Ethiopian CRC patients and to assess the robustness and interpretability of Cox proportional hazard model (Cox PH model), stratified Cox proportional hazard model, frailty model, and Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) models, focusing on model adequacy under assumption violations. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 161 colorectal cancer patients diagnosed between 2012 and 2016. Survival probabilities were estimated using Kaplan–Meier analysis, with group comparisons via log-rank tests. Multivariable modeling employed Cox proportional hazards, stratified Cox proportional hazard model, frailty, and accelerated failure time models. Model adequacy was evaluated through Akaike Information Criterion, concordance indices, and the Global Schoenfeld test for proportional hazards assessment. Results The Cox proportional hazard model violated the proportional hazards assumption (global p = 0.043), primarily due to histological subtype effects, indicating that the standard Cox proportional hazard model was not appropriate for this dataset. Assumption violations were mitigated using the stratified Cox proportional hazard model (global p = 0.122). Among accelerated failure time models, the log-logistic distribution provided superior model fit (AIC = 649.88; concordance = 0.724). Time-ratio (TR) interpretation showed that surgery extended survival by approximately 2.4-fold, whereas elevated baseline carcinoembryonic antigen levels and metastatic disease reduced survival duration by nearly half. Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen, distant metastasis, vascular invasion, and squamous cell histology were consistently associated with poorer prognosis, while surgery and chemotherapy remained protective across models. Conclusion Rigorous model checking indicates that the conventional Cox proportional hazards model is inappropriate for this cohort due to proportional hazard assumption violations. Accelerated failure time modeling, particularly the log-logistic form, offered improved fit and clearer time-based interpretation of covariate effects. These findings underscore the importance of model validation in CRC survival research and highlight the need for improved early detection, surgical access, and targeted management of aggressive tumor subtypes to enhance patient outcomes in Ethiopia.
n43bf38e02cda: The global rise of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens has increased interest in bee-derived natural products as sources of novel antimicrobials. While most research has focused on European honey bee (Apis mellifera) products, the 550 species of stingless bees found globally also produce honey and other hive products, representing a largely unexplored source of novel bioactives. This study investigates the antimicrobial activity of propolis extracts and honey from the Australian stingless bee Tetragonula carbonaria against 16 clinically significant bacterial and fungal pathogens, using broth microdilution methodology. T. carbonaria propolis and honey exhibited distinct antimicrobial profiles: propolis showed selective activity against a subset of bacteria and certain filamentous fungi, while honey showed broad-spectrum activity against all tested bacteria and selective activity against dermatophyte fungi. The level of H2O2 production in T. carbonaria honey was only moderately correlated with its antimicrobial activity, and the total phenolic content of propolis did not correlate significantly with its antimicrobial activity, suggesting other bee- or plant-derived compounds are important contributors. These findings highlight T. carbonaria propolis and honey as promising antimicrobials and potential sources of novel bioactive compounds.
n869bec18ad90: Background Optimal mucosal visualization is essential for high-quality esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), particularly for the detection of subtle upper gastrointestinal lesions. Oral simethicone and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) are commonly used to improve mucosal cleanliness, whereas lidocaine ice popsicles provide effective topical pharyngeal anesthesia for unsedated EGD. We evaluated whether incorporating simethicone and NAC into a lidocaine ice popsicle could improve mucosal visibility while maintaining patient comfort. Methods This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 374 adults undergoing unsedated diagnostic EGD between December 2024 and June 2025. Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive either a lidocaine ice popsicle containing simethicone (100 mg) and NAC (600 mg) or a conventional lidocaine ice popsicle. The primary outcome was mucosal visibility assessed using a modified Total Visibility Score (TVS). Secondary outcomes included procedure time, water volume required for mucosal cleansing, additional simethicone use, endoscopist satisfaction, ease of esophageal instrumentation, gag reflex, patient satisfaction, discomfort, pain, and adverse events. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Results All 374 randomized participants (187 per group) completed the study and were analyzed according to their assigned groups. Baseline characteristics were descriptively similar between groups. The intervention group had a significantly lower TVS than the control group (6.19 ± 0.51 vs. 10.39 ± 2.22; mean difference, −4.20; 95% CI, −4.53 to −3.88; P < 0.001), indicating better mucosal visibility. Exploratory segment-specific analyses showed lower visibility scores in all six gastrointestinal segments. The intervention group also had higher endoscopist satisfaction, shorter procedure time (10.87 ± 1.44 vs. 12.75 ± 0.96 min; P < 0.001), lower water requirements for mucosal cleansing, and less frequent use of additional diluted simethicone during EGD (12.8% vs. 96.8%; P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses showed statistically significant differences in gag reflex and pain scores, although the absolute differences were small. Patient satisfaction, discomfort, and ease of esophageal instrumentation did not differ significantly between groups. No adverse events were observed during the defined observation period. Conclusions The combined formulation of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine incorporated into a lidocaine ice popsicle improved mucosal visibility compared with a lidocaine ice popsicle alone during unsedated EGD and was associated with improved procedural efficiency. This integrated formulation may provide a practical approach to pre-endoscopic preparation by combining topical anesthesia with mucosal cleansing. Further multicenter studies are warranted to confirm its effectiveness, generalizability, and safety with longer follow-up. Trial registration Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20240606004
n45519d6d7829: The preschool years are a critical period for the rapid development of executive function in children. While executive function in preschool children is influenced by multiple factors, existing research has been limited by its theoretical and empirical perspectives, resulting in singular pathways for promoting executive function. To address this, the study adopted a systems theory perspective to explore the configurational pathways through which subsystems of gross motor skills are associated with higher levels of executive function in preschoolers. The study included test data from 67 children aged 3–6 years. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), six subsystems of gross motor skills (running, jumping, throwing, catching, kicking, and striking) were treated as antecedent conditions to explore the configurational associations of gross motor skill subsystems with executive function. Necessary condition analysis indicated that no single gross motor skill subsystem constituted a necessary condition for higher executive function in preschool children. Subsequent configurational analysis identified three distinct pathways that are associated with higher levels of executive function (with a total consistency of 0.906 and an overall coverage of 0.496). The development of executive function in preschool children is not associated with single gross motor actions in a linear manner but rather with multiple concurrent combinations of gross motor skill subsystems characterized by “multiple concurrent pathways leading to the same goal.” This is reflected in the three configurational pathways: “a combination of jumping, throwing, and striking actions,” “a combination of running, kicking, and striking actions,” and “a combination of running, throwing, and catching actions.” These findings provide preliminary insights and hypothesis-generating evidence for future research on gross motor skill activities and executive function development in preschool children.
n8775d42794a6: by Victoria S. Coward, Nalan Gokgoz, Kim M. Tsoi, Jay S. Wunder, Irene L. Andrulis Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma (UPS) is a genetically complex type of soft tissue sarcoma (STS) and there are few therapeutic options for advanced disease. Immune checkpoint blockade therapy may be of benefit to a subset of UPS patients, particularly those with elevated tumoral Programmed Cell Death Ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and an inflamed tumour microenvironment. From transcriptomic analyses we previously identified Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 1 (STAT1) expression, a key mediator of interferon-γ (IFN-γ) signaling, as enriched in a cohort of UPS cases with elevated PD-L1 levels that were observed to have an improved clinical outcome. This led us to investigate the role of STAT1 in UPS biology. We examined the effects of STAT1 loss, and overexpression of either wild type or tyrosine phosphorylation-deficient STAT1 in primary human UPS cell lines. We observed that IFN-γ treatment decreased cell counts, increased cell death, and induced the secretion of CXCR3 ligands in a STAT1-dependent manner. Overexpression of wild type STAT1, but not a tyrosine to phenylalanine phospho-mutant (Y701F), restored IFN-γ-mediated cell death and cytokine secretion, highlighting the importance of Y701 phosphorylation in STAT1-associated antitumour functions. STAT1 Y701 phosphorylation status was associated with gene expression changes that were cell line specific. Together, these findings shed light on the central role of STAT1, and specifically the Y701 phosphorylation, in mediating IFN-γ signaling and related phenotypes. This study underscores the need for further exploration of the role of STAT1 phosphorylation in tumor-immune interactions within UPS.
ne4a0bc6eee21: Beech leaf disease, caused by the invasive foliar nematode Litylenchus crenatae, is an emerging threat to Fagus grandifolia across North America. Since its initial detection in 2012, the disease has spread to a total of 16 U.S. states and the Canadian Province of Ontario; however, the mechanisms underlying nematode dispersal remain poorly understood. This study evaluated multiple potential dispersal pathways across two forest sites in central Pennsylvania through integrated field surveys, environmental monitoring, and experimental validation. Weekly sampling was conducted to characterize nematode population dynamics in relation to temperature, precipitation, wind, and humidity. Long distance water-mediated dispersal was assessed through creek sampling, while biotic dispersal was investigated through field sampling from migratory bird feet during high-moisture events and a controlled greenhouse transmission experiment. Wind dispersal was further examined in a pilot study using unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted rainwater collection during precipitation events. Nematode presence was detected across all investigated pathways, supporting dispersal via water flow, rain splash, and biotic vectors. Funnel-based sampling recovered Litylenchus crenatae up to 90 m from infected trees, demonstrating movement beyond the immediate canopy area. Confirmed downstream transport of nematodes suggests waterways may facilitate long-distance dispersal across forested landscapes. Litylenchus crenatae was recovered from the feet of migratory birds, and greenhouse experiments confirmed that bird-associated nematodes could infect healthy beech seedlings, providing evidence for avian-mediated transmission. Desiccation assays demonstrated that live Litylenchus crenatae specimens could survive up to 10 days in the absence of available moisture, indicating that the nematodes may remain viable during transport on bird feet or exposed surfaces. In addition, unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted rainwater sampling detected Litylenchus crenatae within canopy-associated precipitation samples, providing additional evidence for short-distance aerial dispersal during wind and rain events. Together, these findings demonstrate that beech leaf disease spread is driven by multiple interacting abiotic and biotic dispersal mechanisms operating across spatial scales.
nb45012d98ac2: Nutrient resorption is a key plant strategy for nutrient conservation, yet whether it responds plastically to non-nutrient stressors such as salinity remains unresolved. Using a common garden experiment with 110 genotypes of the cosmopolitan grass Phragmites australis, we first established that the imposed salinity treatment induced strong multilevel stress responses: above-ground biomass declined by >60%, sodium accumulated three- to fivefold across all leaf stages, and 484 metabolites showed significant differential accumulation, including canonical markers of osmotic and oxidative stress. Against this backdrop of confirmed stress, we found that nutrient resorption efficiency (NuRE) remained largely unaffected by salinity. Instead, NuRE was strongly correlated with phylogeographic lineage, ecotype, and latitude of origin, demonstrating evolutionary canalization rather than short-term acclimation. Element-specific regulatory patterns were also evident: while phosphorus resorption followed concentration-dependent control regardless of stress, nitrogen control was disrupted under salinity, and potassium resorption showed no such dependence. Our findings reveal that intraspecific variation in nutrient resorption is predominantly shaped by historical adaptation and geographic context, not by plasticity to salinity. This genetic canalization of a key functional trait implies that predictions of nutrient cycling under global change must account for the phylogeographic composition of plant populations.
n3e98ebe5bbd3: As developing neural circuits become functional, they undergo a phase of heightened plasticity that facilitates network tuning in response to intrinsic and/or extrinsic stimuli. These developmental windows are termed critical periods (CPs) because perturbations during but not outside the CP can lead to lasting changes, such as the formation of sub-optimal or unstable networks. How separate but connected elements within a network might respond differently to a CP perturbation is not well understood. To study this, we used the locomotor network of the Drosophila larva as a model and heat stress as a CP stimulus that has ecological relevance. When embryos experienced heat stress, the subsequent development of their locomotor network was changed, creating larvae with reduced crawling speed and decreased network stability. Developing body wall muscles and central neurons are sensitive to heat stress perturbations during distinct, consecutive phases of embryogenesis. Within the CNS, transient embryonic CP perturbation leads to increased synaptic drive from premotor interneurons to motoneurons, which in turn adopt reduced excitability. In contrast, the peripheral neuromuscular junction maintains normal synaptic transmission, despite significant structural changes. Thus, connected elements respond differentially to a CP perturbation, suggesting a sequence, or hierarchy of network adjustment during the CP.
n5f1052fbb9df: Visualizing the structures of small proteins and complexes has been a longstanding challenge in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). Some of these targets have been successfully resolved by binding to antibody fragments (Fabs) or fusing with external scaffolds to increase their size. Recent advances in conventional single-particle techniques have enabled the determination of an increasing number of structures smaller than 100 kDa, achieving resolutions relevant to drug research. Compared to X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM preserves the near-native states of biomolecules, can resolve structural heterogeneity, and has the potential to apply to a wide range of targets. In this work, we demonstrate that the alignment and reconstruction of small macromolecular complexes can be improved using high-resolution structures as priors, combined with 2D template matching. Using this method, we reconstructed a previously intractable ∼43 kDa protein kinase and improved the density of its ligand-binding site. Our theoretical analysis predicts that this method can further extend single-particle cryo-EM to important drug-binding complexes well below 50 kDa.
n34636b57b955: Hepatocytes undergo extensive proliferation to facilitate liver repair after injury, yet early adaptive changes prior to proliferation remain unclear. Using a mouse model of acetaminophen (APAP)-induced liver injury, we show that hepatocytes undergo transient proliferation suppression that is most pronounced in mid-zone hepatocytes, consistent with zonal APAP metabolism. Although spatial transcriptomics (ST) alone could not independently confirm zonal proliferative restraint, ST analysis identified a unique mid-zone stress-response program centered on the Atf4-Chop axis. By integrating Cut&Run with immunohistochemistry and functional studies, we found that the Atf4-Chop axis suppresses proliferation via the cell-cycle inhibitor Btg2. Together, our findings support a model in which mid-zone hepatocytes transiently prioritize stress adaptation over proliferation, thereby preserving regenerative capacity for subsequent liver repair.
n67157421fd0e: Optogenetic tools are indispensable for understanding the causal neural mechanisms underlying animal behavior, providing millisecond-precision control over genetically defined neural populations. Random-access laser-scanning optogenetics is a powerful and underutilized method for transiently manipulating cortical activity in mice. Despite the utility of this technique, no general-purpose open-source implementation currently exists, and potential users need expertise across optics, real-time hardware control, and programming. This represents a major barrier to adoption, particularly for newly established research groups. Here we present ‘Zapit’, the first open-source general-purpose platform for random-access laser-scanning optogenetic experiments in head-fixed mice. Zapit is fully documented, has a user-friendly GUI, works in stereotaxic coordinates, and comes with easy-to-build hardware options that extend functionality beyond any published system. We validate Zapit’s performance through electrophysiological recordings and cortical photoinhibition in behaving mice. Zapit is a novel and innovative tool with the potential to democratize laser-scanning optogenetics and significantly increase uptake throughout the scientific community.
n7addc66065b1: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) is a key antiviral target that equilibrates between an active dimer and inactive monomer, making the dimerization interface a promising therapeutic vulnerability. This study investigates Mpro monomer-dimer equilibrium and conformational changes induced by inhibitor binding using 13C labeling with native mass spectrometry and hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS). We evaluated how peptidomimetic inhibitors (PF-07321332, PF-00835231, GC376, boceprevir) and non-peptidomimetic inhibitors (carmofur, ebselen, MR6-31-2, AT7519, pelitinib) influence Mpro dimerization and subunit exchange. Key findings revealed divergent mechanisms: peptidomimetic inhibitors significantly shifted the equilibrium towards the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange dynamics and rigidifying the dimer interface; in contrast, ebselen impaired dimer formation and increased interface flexibility. Notably, tandem mass spectrometry identified a novel covalent binding site for ebselen at C300. Molecular dynamics simulations and mutational analyses demonstrated that this C300 modification allosterically alters the hydrogen bond network of the dimer interface, directly contributing to ebselen-mediated dimer disruption and enzymatic inhibition. Overall, this study clarifies distinct inhibitory modes between peptidomimetics and ebselen, highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting allosteric sites at the dimer interface for designing next-generation Mpro inhibitors.
n6c8eb0508434: The evolutionary arms race between plants and insects involves not only direct defense and counter-defense but also sophisticated resource manipulation. However, how herbivorous insects respond to host nutritional signals to modulate their fitness traits remains unclear. This study investigates how the small brown planthopper (SBPH, Laodelphax striatellus) manipulates host plant carbohydrate allocation, and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which the acquired glucose enhances SBPH fecundity and insecticide tolerance. Using molecular, pharmacological, and biochemical approaches, we found that SBPH infestation induced systemic carbohydrate reallocation in rice, elevating whole-plant glucose levels by promoting aerial accumulation while depleting root reserves. Host-derived glucose enhanced SBPH fecundity by activating the target of rapamycin (TOR) pathway, upregulating juvenile hormone (JH) signaling, and increasing vitellogenin production. For imidacloprid tolerance, glucose boosted glutathione S-transferase (GST) activity via two synergistic mechanisms: by upregulating glutamate cysteine ligase (GCL) to increase glutathione synthesis, and transcriptionally via the glucose-TOR-JH axis to induce LsGSTe1 (SBPH epsilon class GST) and LsGSTo1 (SBPH omega class GST) expression. Our findings establish host-derived glucose as a central signaling molecule that SBPH utilizes to modulate conserved pathways for simultaneous optimization of reproduction and insecticide resistance. This reveals a multifaceted nutrient-responsive mechanism in insect pests and identifies the glucose-TOR-JH axis as critical molecular targets for developing nutrient-based pest control strategies, such as disrupting insect nutrient-sensing pathways or modulating host carbohydrate metabolism.
n2d3bfbd3d4b4: In young animals, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) in the CNS efficiently differentiate into myelinating oligodendrocytes (OLs), whereas ageing reduces this capacity, impairing remyelination following demyelinating injury and adaptive myelination involved in learning. To identify factors that restore resilience in aged OPCs, we developed gSWITCH (https://altoslabs.shinyapps.io/gSWITCH/, https://github.com/Tanay-math/gSWITCH), a computational pipeline that captures dynamic gene-expression patterns to identify ‘switch’ genes during lineage progression and ordered biological transitions, including time-series experiments. gSWITCH identified OPC-characteristic switch genes, which we compared between young and aged OPCs to determine whether their regulation is altered with ageing. This revealed several transcription factors with reduced expression in aged OPCs. Transcription-factor binding-site enrichment highlighted Bcl11a as a potential master-regulator of multiple switch genes. Bcl11a inhibition reduced OPC differentiation into OLs, whereas its overexpression in aged OPCs significantly enhanced OL differentiation without affecting proliferation. In aged mice subjected to demyelination injury in spinal cord white matter, Bcl11a overexpression increased OPC differentiation within lesions. We found that Bcl11a has undergone pervasive purifying selection throughout vertebrate evolution, preserving its amino acid sequence by eliminating deleterious mutations. Our study shows that reversing the age-related decline of this evolutionarily conserved factor in aged OPCs restores their impaired capacity for differentiation.
n88df928e4c65: Quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in many aspects of condensed matter physics. Among its central objects are the Berry curvature and the quantum metric—quantities that, while distinct, are intertwined through geometric constraints. In this article, we survey recent progress in understanding when and how this bound is saturated, with particular emphasis on the emergence of momentum-space holomorphicity of Bloch states. These developments highlight a profound connection between certain ideal Bloch bands and the Hilbert space structure of the lowest Landau level. We elucidate this relationship through a review of quantum Hall physics in both homogeneous and spatially varying magnetic fields and conclude by exploring its implications for the search for fractionalized phases in emerging platforms, including moiré materials.
n9a95df70102a: This article is a gentle stroll through the field of optimization and optimal control, aiming to acquaint the reader with the evolution of developments leading up to the Pontryagin maximum principle. The exposition adheres to simplicity without sacrificing integrity. The continuous versions of results are derived as limits of discrete versions, thus adopting a unified approach to finite-dimensional and function spaces, and wherever permissible, an intuitive connection to physics is established. Complete proofs are not provided; instead, the key geometric ideas in the proofs are presented.
n655877e57217: Invasive exotic arthropods and weeds pose a growing threat to biodiversity, food security, and the functioning of whole ecosystems, resulting in significant socioeconomic and ecological impacts. Classical biological control—the importation of specialist natural enemies from the native range—can lead to long-term, sustainable pest suppression, but it is typically implemented reactively after the invasive species is established and is causing significant negative impacts. Proactive biological control offers an anticipatory approach, developing biological control agents before or shortly after establishment and enabling rapid response to new incursions. This review examines current applications, opportunities, and challenges of proactive strategies and proposes steps to advance proactive management of invasive arthropod pests and weeds.
nfd78a74cc8d9: T cell receptor–engineered T (TCR-T) cell therapy has emerged as a promising adoptive cellular therapy for solid tumors by enabling recognition of intracellular antigens presented via human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules. Unlike chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy, TCR-T cell therapy targets a broader antigen repertoire, including cancer-testis antigens, neoantigens, and viral antigens. Recent clinical advances, highlighted by the approval of afamitresgene autoleucel in synovial sarcoma, demonstrate meaningful antitumor activity. However, several limitations remain, including HLA restriction, antigen heterogeneity, toxicity related to on-target/off-tumor effects, and mechanisms of resistance such as antigen loss and T cell exhaustion. Advances in antigen selection, gene editing, and synthetic biology are improving both safety and efficacy. Combination strategies and next-generation engineered constructs are expected to overcome current barriers. This review summarizes the biological rationale, clinical evidence, safety considerations, and resistance mechanisms of TCR-T cell therapy in solid tumors and discusses future directions to optimize their therapeutic potential.
n789e4ad2e301: Bacteria use membraneless compartments, or biomolecular condensates, to organize cellular processes in space and time. These condensates assemble and function within a highly constrained physical landscape shaped by a crowded cytoplasm, structured nucleoid, membrane surfaces, and distinct polar zones. In this review, we examine condensates involved in genome maintenance, RNA metabolism, cell division, signaling, and metabolic regulation, focusing on how cellular microenvironments and physiological state shape when and where these condensates form, which molecules they recruit, and the material states they adopt. In turn, condensates can concentrate molecules for biochemical reactions, sequester them for storage or protection, release or redistribute them as conditions change, and position them at specific cellular sites. Disentangling the contribution of the condensed state from that of the underlying molecular interactions will be essential for determining how condensates regulate bacterial physiology.
nbe59f49b00ea: Eppur si muove —the work of Galileo Galilei marked the beginning of the quantitative study of motion for scope-observable entities. Extending this physics-based perspective to the microscope-observable microbial world has uncovered principles of motion that diverge sharply from our everyday intuition, revealing physics as being essential to understanding microbial motility. In this review, we explore the fundamental physical principles that enable and constrain the motility strategies evolved by diverse microorganisms, with a focus on prokaryotes, to enable propulsion in fluids and along surfaces. We examine how microbial motility functions in complex, heterogeneous environments, and we provide a brief evolutionary perspective on microbial motility by highlighting its costs and benefits. In summary, we show how including a physical approach in the study of microbial motility both unveils general solutions and specific adaptations and enables a better understanding of a world for which our intuition is not trained.
n0147da51a5b2: Peptides are among the smallest functional biomolecules. Learning to systematically design their activity would revolutionize biology and medicine. Yet achieving this goal remains an open challenge. Recent advances in machine learning enable the discovery and design of peptides at scale, not only yielding new antibiotic agents effective against priority pathogens but also revealing unexpected roles for peptides in host immunity. In this review, we survey how artificial intelligence (AI) methods can be used to mine genomes, proteomes, and even ancient sequence data to uncover “encrypted” peptide antibiotics across the tree of life and over evolutionary time. We highlight emerging approaches for activity prediction, structure–activity modeling, sequence optimization, and de novo peptide generation, and we discuss workflows that tightly couple in silico design with high-throughput experimental validation. We further introduce the concept of “encrypted immunity,” in which ordinary proteins encode latent antimicrobial fragments, and we outline translational opportunities as well as remaining challenges on the path to bringing AI-designed peptides to the clinic.
n01db1bbde499: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria are common in natural environments, including the microbiota of animal and human hosts. The local physical, chemical, and biological conditions of environmental patches and matrices vary both qualitatively and quantitatively. Often, these conditions are found as gradients, creating intersections that can either facilitate or inhibit the spread and evolution of antibiotic resistance (AbR). Ecological kinetics (EcoK) describes how combinations of these conditions influence the abundance and transmission of antibiotic-resistant populations, as well as the mobile genetic elements that carry resistance genes. Evolutionary dynamics (EvoD) concerns the effects of environmental conditions on genetic variation, the expression of resistance traits, and the evolvability of host bacteria, ultimately contributing to the emergence and selection of AbR. This review examines the influence of numerous environmental conditions on EcoK and EvoD. This field remains poorly understood, and further research is essential to identify high-risk areas where surveillance for the emergence and spread of AbR should be implemented.
n0c668217e858: In all living cells, chemical reactions known as metabolism generate energy and building blocks for cellular structures. Metabolism produces and consumes ATP, the major currency of cellular energy. Because approximately 85% of ATP is bound to Mg 2+ , bacteria reduce their ATP concentration when cytoplasmic Mg 2+ availability drops below a certain threshold. This reduction in ATP concentration reshapes metabolism and gene transcription as well as protein synthesis, solubility, and turnover. This article reviews how ATP acts both directly and via ATP-derived signaling molecules, such as 3′,5′-cyclic AMP (cAMP), bis-(3′,5′)-cyclic dimeric-AMP (c-di-AMP), diadenosine tetraphosphate (Ap 4 A), and guanosine-3′,5′-tetra- and pentaphosphate [(p)ppGpp], which direct adaptations to stresses bacteria experience in their natural environments. It also discusses how Mg 2+ -responsive regulatory systems supersede canonical control of metabolism and protein homeostasis by governing ATP amounts and how this bacterial response slows growth, modifies cell envelope structures, and favors survival.
n6bce9b30997a: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies marked a major breakthrough in obesity pharmacotherapy, while subsequent advancements targeting multiple entero-pancreatic hormones now deliver weight loss previously achievable only with bariatric surgery, alongside improvements in obesity-related complications. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including reduced efficacy in diabetic populations, gastrointestinal adverse effects, and high costs that drive a real-world adherence gap. Consequently, next-generation therapies, including receptor polyagonists, oral formulations, and small-molecule incretin mimetics with optimized pharmacokinetic profiles, are being developed to enhance efficacy, tolerability, and accessibility while maintaining safety. However, weight regain after treatment cessation remains a critical hurdle. Growing evidence underscores the importance of sustained lifestyle interventions and muscle mass preservation to facilitate weight stabilization. Concurrently, research is heavily focused on identifying the biological drivers of weight regain, such as altered neuroregulation, metabolic adaptation, and adipose tissue remodeling. This review examines the current landscape, limitations, and emerging strategies of obesity pharmacotherapy.
n2e3bfb7ddc8f: Bone is a hierarchical and heterogeneous bio-composite material, with cortical and trabecular regions exhibiting distinct mechanical behaviors across scales. Patient-specific Finite Element Analysis (FEA) derived from medical images is increasingly used in both human and veterinary medicine to predict bone mechanical behavior under various loading conditions, assess fracture risk, and evaluate treatment outcomes. However, due to the complexity associated with measuring full elasto-plastic bone properties across multiple scales and bridging microscale properties to macroscale models, simplified material definitions are often adopted in FEA simulations. Such simplifications may produce unrealistic mechanical responses and fail to capture permanent microscopic and macroscopic deformations that occur when stresses exceed the bone yield point, particularly in implant design applications. This study presents an integrated experimental–computational framework for generating continuum material maps as a function of density from tissue-scale characterization of the canine femur. High-depth spherical nanoindentation combined with Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based inverse optimization was conducted to extract mechanically consistent elasto-plastic properties of cortical and trabecular bone from load–displacement responses influenced by post-yield contact uncertainties. Trabecular tissue-scale properties were then assigned to Representative Volume Elements (RVEs) reconstructed from micro-Quantitative Computed Tomography (μQCT) data and homogenized to account for architecture-dependent effective behavior. Finally, optimized cortical and homogenized trabecular properties were correlated with density to establish compartment-specific material mapping relationships for whole-bone FEA simulations. The optimized responses showed good agreement with the experimental indentation measurements, supporting the capability of the proposed framework to generate mechanically informed material definitions for patient-specific bone FEA simulations. Overall, the proposed framework provides a pathway for translating localized experimental measurements into heterogeneous elasto-plastic material inputs for whole-bone FEA without explicitly resolving trabecular microarchitecture.

n7bb1231a501d: Background This study translated, culturally adapted, and evaluated the First Aid Willingness Questionnaire for Schoolchildren to assess adolescents’ self-reported readiness to help and potential barriers to first-aid provision. Methods This cross-sectional psychometric study included 470 high school students in Aksaray, Türkiye. The questionnaire underwent forward–backward translation, review by 12 experts, and pilot testing with 35 students. Exploratory factor analysis derived the structure, which was subsequently evaluated via ordinal confirmatory factor analysis in the same sample. Content and construct validity, internal consistency, and measurement invariance across gender, grade level, and perceived family income were assessed. Results All item-level content validity ratios exceeded 0.83; the scale-level content validity index was 0.90. Removing two items yielded a 16-item, three-factor structure: First Aid Willingness, Negative Emotions, and Perceived Knowledge. The model showed acceptable fit: scaled χ²(101) = 288.09, p < 0.001; comparative fit index = 0.95; Tucker–Lewis index = 0.94; root mean square error of approximation = 0.06, 90% confidence interval [0.05, 0.07]; standardized root mean square residual = 0.06. Composite reliability ranged from 0.79 to 0.90. Average variance extracted ranged from 0.49 to 0.59, with borderline convergent validity for Negative Emotions. Discriminant validity was supported. Cronbach’s alpha ranged from 0.72 to 0.87, and McDonald’s omega from 0.74 to 0.87. Configural, threshold, metric, and scalar invariance were supported across all grouping variables. Strict invariance was supported across grade level and perceived family income, but not gender. Conclusion The results provide preliminary evidence for the Turkish questionnaire’s psychometric properties and support subscale interpretation and latent mean comparisons within the study sample. Independent replication and evaluation of temporal stability, responsiveness, and external validity are needed.
n1b74a46a6268: Due to their low signal-to-noise ratio and non-stationarity, accurately classifying EEG signals is still one of the main hindrances that limit the real-world applications of a brain-computer interface (BCI). Deep learning (DL) is a potential method for addressing the problem. However, how to create a suitable DL network for motor imagery (MI)-based BCIs poses severe challenges in the case of insufficient training data. In this paper, a DL network based on multiscale convolutional neural network (CNN) and temporal and channel attention mechanisms is proposed for decoding MI tasks. Temporal and spatial features are extracted by four parallel CNN branches, each of which is followed by a Transformer block for learning the global correlations of local time features. The outputs from the four Transformer blocks are concatenated along channel dimension and then input into a channel attention module for channel fusion. The subsequent feature map is classified by a CNN, which replaces the commonly used fully connected layer for reducing computational complexity. The proposed network was evaluated on three publicly available BCI datasets and compared with five state-of-the-art DL networks. The training data sets are augmented using the approach segmentation and reconstruction. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed network achieved an average accuracy of 80.21% on Dataset 1 (4-class tasks), 90.19% on Dataset 2 (2-class tasks), and 97.32% on Dataset 3 (4-class tasks), surpassing the strongest baselines FBCNet on Dataset 1, MSFBCNN on Dataset 2 and MSFBCNN on Dataset 3 by 2.59%, 1.27%, and 1.99% respectively. The network effectively decoded the MI-based EEG signals, providing a potential method for BCI applications.
n8036ff01abf1: Leaf day respiratory rate (Rd), a pivotal component of plant carbon metabolism that directly modulates net photosynthetic carbon gain and plant fitness, has long been challenging to accurately quantify due to overlapping CO2 fluxes with photosynthesis and photorespiration (Rp). This study aimed to disentangle Rd from Rp in C3 crops using a high-CO2/low-O2 (>1200 μmol mol–1 CO2 + 2% O2) An/Ca (net photosynthetic rate-ambient CO2 concentration) model. We integrated two datasets: An/Ca curve data of four C3 species (Trifolium pratense, Silphium perfoliatum, Lolium perenne, Triticum aestivum) under ambient O2 (21% O2) from Ye et al. (2025) and newly collected data under low O2 (2% O2) for the same species. A dedicated model (Eqn 1) was developed to extract key parameters [e.g., the maximum net photosynthetic rate (Anmax), CO2 compensation point (Γ) in the presence of Rd, photorespiratory rate at Ca = 0 μmol mol–1 (RC0)] from An/Ca curves, with ANOVA confirming no significant differences between calculated and observed parameter values (p > 0.05). Under 2% O2, Rp was strongly suppressed, making the gross photorespiratory rate (RC = Rp + Rd) a reliable proxy for approximate Rd. Results showed that Rd estimates from the high-CO2/low-O2 approach (0.74–1.12 μmol m–2 s–1) were consistent with literature ranges (0.74–2.89 μmol m–2 s–1) for four C3 crops. Interspecific differences in Rd were observed: L. perenne had the highest Rd, while T. aestivum had the lowest, which correlated with species-specific photosynthetic traits (e.g., carboxylation efficiency). Rd remained stable across O2 levels (21% vs. 2%), indicating independence from short-term photorespiratory flux changes. The RC ≈ Rd assumption is supported by the substantial decrease in Γ (50–67%) and RCO (40–55%) under 2% O2, and by the consistency of Rd estimates with literature ranges, although independent ground-truth measurements remain to be conducted. This study suggests the high-CO2/low-O2 An/Ca model as a new tool for Rd quantification in C3 crops. The findings enhance understanding of non-photosynthetic carbon flux dynamics and provide critical parameters for refining crop carbon cycling models to predict growth and yield under current and future atmospheric conditions.
n573f4e19954d: Background Since 2015, oral emergency contraceptives (ECs) have been available in German community pharmacies without prescription as over-the-counter medicines. Given the financial burden, unnecessary hormonal exposure and associated side effects, systematic information gathering is crucial to prevent unnecessary recommendations. This study aimed to determine whether pharmacy staff ask the checklist questions recommended by the German Federal Chamber of Pharmacists (BAK) guideline and provide correct recommendations when oral EC is not indicated (appropriate outcome), and to examine associated factors. Methods A nationwide study using the simulated patient methodology – considered the “gold standard” – was conducted with a stratified random sample of 376 community pharmacies across Germany. Eight trained female mystery callers aged 21–24 simulated a scenario in which a combined oral contraceptive was forgotten once after sexual intercourse. However, the pill could still be taken within the 12-hour window, making oral EC unnecessary according to the BAK guideline. To ensure quality, each call was monitored by a second observer. Results Of 376 mystery calls conducted, 322 were included in the primary analysis. An appropriate outcome was achieved in 44.4% (143/322), while oral EC was unnecessarily recommended in 49.1% (158/322). The median questioning score was 2.0 of 4.0 points. A multivariable logistic regression model showed that a higher questioning score and mystery caller identity were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome. Qualitative findings indicated both positive counseling practices and notable deficiencies among pharmacy staff. Conclusion The results show deficits in information gathering and appropriate recommendations. To improve counseling, the consistent use of the BAK checklist during telephone consultations should be explicitly recommended in the relevant guideline. Targeted training for pharmacy staff may help address professional and communication deficits. Surprisingly, some mystery callers were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome, highlighting the need for further research on the influence of vocal characteristics and last names in telephone consultations.
ndfe4e55cb195: Banana breeding programs prioritize improving yield with resistance to biotic stresses while maintaining fruit quality. This study focused on identifying genotypes with resistance to five major biotic constraints including Cosmopolites sordidus, Radopholus similis, banana Xanthomonas wilt, Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense – Race 1 and Pseudocercospora fijiensis. A diverse set of diploid and tetraploid genotypes was phenotyped under controlled screenhouse and field conditions to identify potential sources of. A partially replicated (P-rep) design, was used to accommodate unequal plant availability arising from asynchronous multiplication. P-rep design enabled robust phenotypic comparisons and identification of genotypes expressing resistance to multiple biotic stresses. Several diploid genotypes exhibited resistance to multiple constraints, highlighting their potential as parental lines for resistance introgression and broadening the genetic base for banana improvement. Leveraging on the efficiency and precision of the P-rep experimental design, these findings accelerate the phenotyping of genotypes.
n730a07c03273: Smartphone mHealth apps (mHealth apps) have played a highly positive role in medical services, which provides a new direction for users’ medical services and health management.
