Using longitudinal qualitative data from Finland, Slovakia and South Korea, this case series examines how individuals who had previously experienced self-identified gaming-related problems reached recovery without successful intervention explicitly targeting their gaming behaviour. Six recurring recovery pathways were identified: axiological shift, social enforcement, gradual regulation, reflexive transformation, healing comorbidity and environmental transformation. Rather than centring on abstinence or direct symptom elimination, recovery emerged through reconfigurations of life structure, social roles and personal value hierarchies. In most cases, gaming did not disappear but was repositioned within a broader ecology of responsibilities and relationships. These findings suggest that natural recovery in GD may be better understood as a contextual and relational reconfiguration rather than solely as symptom reduction. The pathways identified here provide a conceptual stepping stone towards more comprehensive frameworks for understanding the recovery process in GD.
n8aaab5243703: Palladium–iron (Pd–Fe) bimetallic catalysis represents a pivotal strategy for advancing the sustainability of organometallic transformations. Herein, we report a facile and efficient synthetic protocol for Pd–Fe magnetic nanomaterials mediated by carbonyl iron, which proceeds without external reducing agents, surfactants or protective gases. In this approach, carbonyl iron serves a dual role as both the iron source and the reducing agent, while in situ generated carbon monoxide provides three essential functions: atmospheric protection, pressure regulation and crystal nucleus stabilization. This unique reaction system facilitates the co-deposition of zero-valent palladium (Pd0) and iron oxide (Fe2O3) onto pristine Fe3O4 surfaces, yielding magnetically recyclable Pd–Fe@Fe3O4 nanocomposites. Comprehensive characterization via high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirms the well-defined hierarchical structure, uniform elemental distribution and controlled valence states of the as-synthesized materials. The resulting nanomaterials display a narrow particle size distribution (2–3 nm), high metal loading efficiency and low lattice mismatch. Preliminary catalytic evaluations reveal excellent activity of Pd–Fe@Fe3O4 in Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reactions. Notably, similar performance is achieved with catalysts derived from other metal carbonyl precursors, underscoring the generality of this synthetic platform for designing efficient and recyclable bimetallic nanocatalysts.
n0f07f315c00d: Backlash against the artificial intelligence (AI) industry is growing globally in recognition of the high costs and highly uncertain risks borne by society. General-purpose AI systems are sold predominantly on the basis of economic benefits, with little attention given to social or non-financial benefits. Policymakers tasked with regulating AI while balancing European Union (EU) rights and values with innovation and free market competition face a seemingly impossible task. A change of priorities is urgently needed in EU tech policy. Current policy predominantly focuses on risk mitigation rather than delivering socially beneficial technologies. EU tech policy should be rebalanced in favour of societal interests owing to the substantial (in)direct subsidies paid to support the AI industry via tax breaks, public funding, privileged access to public lands, resources, data and infrastructure and widespread deregulation. We propose adding a third goal to rebalance EU AI policy-making: happiness. When policymakers are deciding whether subsidies should be granted for the AI industry, they should require companies to concretely predict measurable benefits for happiness, and hold them accountable for delivering on their predictions. To unpack this proposal, we examine decades of research in psychology to identify key determinants of happiness, focusing on three widely accepted traits: relatedness, competence and autonomy.
nb727a4d0902b: Sustainably closing agricultural yield gaps remains a central challenge for advancing global food security while conserving biodiversity. This article develops a theoretical perspective on why sustainable intensification (SI) is limited in many lower-income countries, despite the technological feasibility of improving yields in these places. It explores these constraints to SI through two case studies of expanding commodity frontiers: (i) beef in the Brazilian Amazon and Cerrado and (ii) cocoa in West Africa. We find similar barriers to SI across the cases, including limited tenurial, financial, knowledge and cultural support, community-level risks to investment and cheap land favouring agricultural expansion. At the same time, both cases reveal potential for rapid intensification, as demonstrated by success in selected locations. The analysis helps explain why many promising SI strategies have achieved limited uptake in countries where land for expansion is still relatively abundant. The article also identifies a more optimistic pathway: ambitious economic and institutional reforms, well-funded community-level technical and financial investments, and smart conservation policies could unlock joint gains for food security and biodiversity. Global policy and finance changes have opened windows for this coordinated policy agenda, but improved demand-side policies are also needed to tip low-yielding agricultural systems onto new trajectories.
n4eb2c71de716: A well-established inverted U-shape relationship links stimulus complexity and human music preference, with preferences peaking at intermediate levels. We investigated whether preference for intermediate complexity is unique to humans or shared with other species. We compared the acoustic preferences of humans and budgerigars, a species known for their vocal learning and pattern recognition abilities, using a three-option place preference paradigm. Participants were presented with choices between stimuli of different, computationally defined complexity: pitch sequences with tones arranged either randomly (high complexity), repeating patterns with changes (medium) or fully repetitive patterns (low). Our results demonstrate that, without specific goals or external rewards, both humans and budgerigars spontaneously exhibit a nonlinear (intermediate) preference profile, indicating a pattern consistent with an inverted U-shape relationship. Because a U-shape relationship may reflect a strategy to seek informative sources maximally useful for learning—that is, for building and refining internal models of the environment—this preference in the acoustic domain may support vocal learning. However, further testing could determine whether it also exists in vocal non-learning species. Because vertebrates show inverted U-shape responses in a variety of non-auditory contexts, our findings may stem from general processes, but potentially depend on vocal learning to translate to acoustic contexts.
nbd8ce6ce9af5: A simple strategy was developed to fabricate self-supporting bioanodes from graphitized palm-tree-branch powder for application in membrane-less microbial fuel cells (MFCs). Palm tree branches were graphitized at 900°C, 1000°C and 1100°C, ground into fine powder, blended with bitumen and starch, compression-moulded and thermally treated to produce robust anodes. The resulting electrodes were evaluated in an air-cathode, single-chamber MFC using raw sewage wastewater without external microbial inoculation or nutrient addition. Structural and electrochemical analyses showed that the prepared anodes possessed rough porous surfaces, stable carbon-dominated electrochemical behaviour and improved conductivity compared with an activated-carbon-based anode. Among the investigated samples, the anode prepared from palm branches graphitized at 1000°C exhibited the best overall performance. In sewage containing 5g l−1 sodium acetate, this anode delivered a maximum power density of about 1300 mW m−2, which was nearly 25 times higher than that of the activated-carbon-based anode (approx. 52 mW m−2). Even under electrolyte-free conditions, the same anode generated a maximum power density of about 400 mW m−2, indicating that intrinsically retained inorganic species, particularly KCl, may contribute to sustaining MFC operation without external electrolyte addition. In contrast, NaCl showed a much weaker promoting effect than sodium acetate. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy confirmed relatively low ohmic and charge-transfer resistances under the optimum condition.
n49ed5391517a: Earthworms (Lumbricidae) are moisture-loving soil-dwellers that can be categorized into two feeding guilds with distinct behaviours: detritivores and geophages. Detritivores feed on litter fragments and geophages on smaller litter particles mixed with soil. When earthworms move within and across soil layers to forage, soil characteristics might influence the scale of these movements and their detectability to predators. To investigate the extent to which the detection of earthworm movements and the vibrations they thereby generate is affected by soil moisture, we used an innovative method to detect and quantify vibrations of moving earthworms emitted through the soil. We designed a mesocosm experiment in which we recorded, with a geophone, the movement-induced vibrations of detritivores and geophages in drier and wetter soils. Earthworm vibrations were detected best at 200 Hz and were detected significantly more in wetter than in drier soils. Moreover, in wetter soils, vibrations induced by detritivores were detected more frequently and at higher intensities than those of geophages. These findings suggest differences in activity levels between detritivores and geophages, as a function of soil moisture content. The observed activity patterns are likely to have food web consequences because earthworm consumers relying on mechanoreceptors to detect prey might detect detritivores more often, specifically in wetter soils.
n690d6e630b73: A newly synthesized azo ligand, 1-((5-allyl-2-hydroxy-3-methoxyphenyl)diazenyl)anthracene-9,10-dione (H-MND), derived from an anthraquinone nucleus coupled with the natural phenol (eugenol), was employed to prepare Co(II), Ni(II), Cu(II), Rh(III) and Pd(II) complexes, with the ligand proposed to adopt a tridentate coordination mode. Anthraquinone derivatives and natural phenols are recognized for diverse pharmacological activities, making them valuable scaffolds for the design of bioactive ligands. The synthesized compounds were characterized by FT-IR, UV–vis, NMR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, elemental analysis, thermal analysis thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TGA-DSC), assessment of chlorine content, magnetic susceptibility and molar conductance measurements, which collectively suggested predominantly non-electrolytic behaviour. In the 1,1-diphenyl-2-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) assay, the Ni(II) complex exhibited the highest antioxidant activity among the synthesized compounds, with an IC50 value significantly different from that of gallic acid (t = 4.31, p ˂ 0.01). Only the Pd(II) complex displayed activity towards plasmid DNA consistent with partial cleavage in the absence of externally added redox agents. Furthermore, activity mimicking phenoxazinone synthase was evaluated for the Cu(II) and Co(II) complexes, revealing system-specific catalytic behaviour. These results support further investigation into the biomedical and catalytic potential of these metal complexes.
n970d7df595d5: Coral reefs deliver vital services via a complex three-dimensional framework sustained by the balance between calcium carbonate production and erosion, or the net carbonate budget state. In many tropical western Atlantic reefs, ecological decline has reduced carbonate production, yielding near-neutral or negative budgets. Yet some reefs retain high coral cover and, theoretically, should also have high net positive budgets, yet often show modest carbonate accumulation. We used the remote reef of Cayo Arenas in the Campeche Bank, Gulf of Mexico, to test whether in reefs under suboptimal (variable) environmental conditions, high coral production is offset by robust bioeroder communities, producing neutral budgets. At 14 sites, we quantified carbonate producers and bioeroders to estimate gross production, bioerosion and net budget states. Despite relatively high live coral cover, mean net carbonate budgets did not differ significantly from a neutral (zero) state, despite a positive net budget (0.7 ± 0.5 SE kg CaCO3 m−2 yr−1) and substantial site-to-site variability (range: −2.3 to 4.3 kg CaCO3 m−2 yr−1). Crucially, this neutrality arose not from depressed biological activity (as in degraded reefs) but from an active equilibrium: elevated carbonate production coupled with substantial bioerosion. These reefs, therefore, represent a contemporary, functional reef state in net stasis. Distinguishing active-neutral reefs, where both production and bioerosion are elevated, from impoverishment-neutral reefs, where both are suppressed, is critical for predicting reef trajectories under environmental change and for targeting management, although near-stasis emerging from high carbonate turnover can appear functionally intact yet operate with limited buffering capacity against net carbonate loss.
ne8920f9bfb49: Cultural traditions shape how animals approach ecological problems. Over the last two decades, Ugandan chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes schweinfurthii) have engaged with the honey-trap experiment, an apparatus mimicking a beehive, while relying on their cultural knowledge. Here, we compared the behaviour of three Ugandan chimpanzee communities in the experiment, adding a previously untested community, the Mwera South chimpanzees of Bugoma Forest. First, we tested whether communities varied in their engagement with the experiment and investigated whether differences lay in individual or community-based characteristics. Second, we analysed individual variation within the same culture, particularly focusing on the new data coming from Bugoma Forest. We found that only the Kanyawara chimpanzees of Kibale Forest displayed a dedicated instrumental method, stick use, realized in their cultural knowledge and expressed by most members of the community, congruent with the largest engagement with the resource and suggestive of a general positive cultural attitude towards honey. By contrast, the two other communities appeared to lack a cultural attitude towards honey, with no attached tool technique overall. Nevertheless, there were also large inter-individual differences. Notably, Bugoma chimpanzees displayed undescribed behavioural flexibility, using a range of tool behaviours, including both stick and leaf tool use, a pattern never documented before. Cultural attitudes toward resources thus constitute an additional layer to culture in addition to instrumental knowledge and coexist with individual motivational traits in influencing the realization of cultural behaviour.
nd1b971a966db: By the mid-twentieth century, the previously booming bird feather trade was a fraction of what it was in its prime, allowing for the recovery of many bird species. We use a qualitative impact evaluation method to assign probable causality to different drivers of this change, ultimately providing expert-supported explanations of how a large-scale behaviour change was enacted to benefit conservation. We outline a method for applying general elimination methodology plus (GEM+), accounting for different facets of evidence reliability, to generate conclusions on most strongly supported causes of change. GEM+ addresses calls for an increase in impact evaluation in conservation, which will require a range of tools, including qualitative, to fill. Analysis of diverse evidence using GEM+ suggests that conservation advocacy, interacting with broader contextual factors, plausibly contributed to a shift in public behaviour that was instrumental in the passage of the Plumage Act and the subsequent end of the trade. This case study has widespread implications for designing effective behaviour change campaigns, as well as providing a framework for conducting impact evaluations in a range of conservation settings.
n5cc5b50de041: Planning is critical for adaptive behaviour in a changing world, because it lets us anticipate the future and adjust our actions accordingly. While prefrontal cortex is crucial for this process, it remains unknown how planning is implemented in neural circuits. Prefrontal representations were recently discovered in simpler sequence memory tasks, where different populations of neurons represent different future time points. We demonstrate that combining such representations with the ubiquitous principle of neural attractor dynamics allows circuits to solve much richer problems, including planning. This is achieved by embedding the environment structure directly in synaptic connections to implement an attractor network that infers desirable futures. The resulting ‘spacetime attractor’ excels at planning in challenging tasks known to depend on the prefrontal cortex. Recurrent neural networks trained by gradient descent on such tasks learn a solution that precisely recapitulates the spacetime attractor – in representation, in dynamics, and in connectivity. Analyses of networks trained across different environment structures reveal a generalisation mechanism that rapidly reconfigures the world model used for planning, without the need for synaptic plasticity. The spacetime attractor is a testable mechanistic theory of planning. If true, it would provide a path towards detailed mechanistic understanding of how prefrontal cortex structures adaptive behaviour.
n92841ace8bd1: Adaptive behavior requires assigning emotional value to sensory cues and generalizing to similar stimuli. The prelimbic cortex (PL) is critical for threat expression and discrimination, yet its neuronal ensembles undergo substantial turnover over time. How stable population codes emerge despite this reorganization remains unknown. Using longitudinal calcium imaging in freely moving mice, we tracked PL activity for 30 days during auditory discriminative fear learning and retrieval. Despite substantial ensemble turnover, stable graded representations persisted in PL populations. A generalized linear model showed that the tone threat value explained graded activity better than freezing, indicating that PL primarily encodes stimulus significance. Population similarity across stimulus presentations was highest for shock-associated and highly generalized tones, suggesting a stable population code underlying threat generalization. Stable neurons preserved graded gradients across sessions, whereas learning modulated the rate of dynamic frequency-selective neurons. Together, these populations enabled stable threat-value coding despite ongoing ensemble reorganization.
nfd8d863c3b3b: Endosymbiotic bacteria can affect many ecological attributes of their insect hosts, including (in herbivorous insects) how they interact with plants where they feed. This raises the issue of whether deliberate endosymbiont introductions could be used to decrease crop damage caused by insect pests. Here, we investigate how transinfecting Rickettsiella viridis and Regiella insecticola endosymbionts into a novel pest aphid host, the Russian wheat aphid (Diuraphis noxia), influences population growth, alate production, dispersal ability, and crop damage. Both the Rickettsiella (originating from pea aphids) and Regiella (from green peach aphids) were stably maintained in their new host where they had contrasting effects. Rickettsiella increased the severity of aphid feeding damage on wheat and barley, resulting in greater leaf loss, chlorotic streaking, and higher aphid populations, whereas Regiella reduced aphid population growth and the severity of feeding damage by aphids. Their effects on dispersal morphology also differed: Regiella had no detectable impact on alate incidence, while Rickettsiella consistently suppressed wing formation in small cages, and in larger mesocosms with multiple wheat plants this endosymbiont suppressed dispersal. Endosymbiont-mediated changes in feeding damage did not involve the main plant immune response pathways: transinfected and wild type aphids induced similar levels of jasmonic acid, jasmonic acid-isoleucine, and salicylic acid in plant tissues, even though these plant defenses were strongly activated during aphid feeding. Novel endosymbionts can therefore modulate the severity of plant feeding damage by aphids as well as influencing aphid dispersal. Potential applications in controlling pest D. noxia populations are discussed.
n6d7777304da1: Ongoing experience is continuously processed in the context of past events. Divergence between current experience and memory-based predictions (i.e., a mnemonic prediction error; MPE) is theorized to be a signal that encoding, as opposed to retrieval, should be prioritized. We asked how MPEs place demands on control and attention-related processes, and whether these demands differ as a function of prediction strength. We investigated these questions across two experiments, wherein we recorded scalp electroencephalography and/or pupillometry as 101 young human adults performed an associative memory task. Strong MPEs, more so than weak MPEs, increased physiological indices of cognitive control (frontal theta), attention (posterior alpha and pupil size), and arousal (pupil size). Greater cognitive control (frontal theta) during strong MPEs promoted better learning of prediction-violating (i.e., unexpected) stimuli. Collectively, these findings reveal multiple pathways through which the mind and brain respond adaptively to violations of strong mnemonic predictions.
nd092406caa9d: Sumoylation is a post-translational modification that can regulate different physiological functions. Increased sumoylation, specifically conjugation of SUMO2/3 (small ubiquitin-like modifier 2/3), is detrimental to vascular health. However, the molecular mechanism mediating this effect is poorly understood. We used cell-based assays and mass spectrometry to show that p66Shc is a direct target of SUMO2 and that SUMO2 regulates p66Shc function via lysine-81 modification. To determine the effects of SUMO2-p66ShcK81 on vascular function, we generated Shc1K81R mice and crossbred them toLdlr-/- mice to induce hyperlipidemia. Next, to determine p66ShcK81-SUMO2ylation-induced changes in endothelial cell signaling, we performed mass spectrometry followed by Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Our data reveal that p66Shc mediates the effects of SUMO2 on endothelial cells. Mass spectrometry identified that SUMO2 modified lysine-81 in the unique collagen homology-2 domain of p66Shc. SUMO2ylation of p66Shc increased phosphorylation at serine-36, causing it to translocate to the mitochondria, a step critical for the oxidative function of p66Shc. Notably, sumoylation-deficient p66Shc (p66ShcK81R) was resistant to SUMO2-induced p66ShcS36 phosphorylation and mitochondrial translocation. Shc1K81R mice were resistant to endothelial dysfunction induced by SUMO2ylation and hyperlipidemia. Ingenuity Pathway Analysis revealed multiple signaling pathways regulated by p66ShcK81-SUMO2ylation in endothelial cells, highlighting JAK-STAT as a major pathway affected by SUMO2-p66ShcK81. Collectively, our work reveals SUMO2-p66Shc signaling as a fundamental regulator of vascular endothelial function. We discovered that p66ShcK81 is an upstream modification regulating p66Shc signaling and mediates hyperlipidemia-induced endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress.
nd29d584f049f: Prison work has become a focus of research in corrections, with studies examining deleterious effects of nearly every aspect of the occupation. Correction officers navigate a variety of organizational and operational stressors within a complex occupational culture. This article identifies potentially harmful aspects of the occupation and reviews empirical findings related to officer well-being, incorporating direct accounts from correction officers. The review highlights prominent stressors that increase risk for adverse behavioral, emotional, and physical and mental health outcomes among officers, including the unique contribution that violence and trauma exposures have on officer mental health and suicide. Developing and offering evidence-based well-being initiatives and leveraging officers’ social support networks are potentially promising mechanisms by which to limit the negative impacts of correctional work. Although a long-term effort, addressing harmful aspects of the occupational culture will benefit correction officers, the incarcerated population, and correctional organizations.
nccfc88e18b60: Genetic evidence implicates immune dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the neuroimmune mechanisms operating in human tissue remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a modular human forebrain organoid platform that systematically integrates human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia and CD8+ T cells to reconstitute multicellular AD pathology. This system enables functional interrogation of both innate and adaptive immune components in a human-relevant context. Using this platform, we demonstrate that microglia mediate amyloid-β clearance and neuronal maturation but also drive inflammatory activation and recruit CD8+ T cells through CCL4/5 signaling via CCR1/5 and CXCR3, establishing a neuroinflammatory feedback loop. Pharmacological targeting of CCR5 or CXCR3 blocks T cell recruitment and modulates autophagy in a microglia-dependent manner. This modular organoid platform provides a versatile tool for dissecting neuron–immune interactions and enables cell-type-specific therapeutic screening in human neuroinflammatory disease models.
n1258831cbbed: A critical phase of mammalian brain development takes place after birth. Neurons of the mouse neocortex undergo dramatic changes in their morphology, physiology, and synaptic connections during the first postnatal month, while properties of immature neurons, such as the capacity for robust axon outgrowth, are lost. The genetic and epigenetic programs controlling prenatal development are well studied, but our understanding of the transcriptional mechanisms that regulate postnatal neuronal maturation is comparatively lacking. By integrating chromatin accessibility and gene expression data from two subtypes of neocortical pyramidal neurons in the neonatal and maturing brain, we predicted a role for the Krüppel-like factor (KLF) family of transcription factors in the developmental regulation of neonatally expressed genes. Using a multiplexed CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) knockdown strategy, we found that a shift in expression from KLF activators (Klf6, Klf7) to repressors (Klf9, Klf13) during early postnatal development functions as a transcriptional ‘switch’ to first activate, then repress a set of shared targets with cytoskeletal functions including Tubb2b and Dpysl3. We demonstrate that this switch is buffered by redundancy between KLF paralogs, which our multiplexed CRISPRi strategy is equipped to overcome and study. Our results indicate that competition between activators and repressors within the KLF family regulates a conserved component of the postnatal maturation program that may underlie the loss of intrinsic axon growth in maturing neurons. This could facilitate the transition from axon growth to synaptic refinement required to stabilize mature circuits.
n0e217fe9b004: Innate T cells, including invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells, mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells, and γδ T cells, bridge innate and adaptive immunity through rapid responses to nonpeptide antigens, metabolites, and stress-associated signals. In cancer, these populations can promote tumor surveillance through cytotoxicity, type 1 cytokine production, tissue-resident immune monitoring, and activation of broader antitumor networks. However, their functions are highly context dependent. Within suppressive tumor microenvironments, tumor-infiltrating unconventional T cell compartments may contain developmentally programmed innate-like subsets together with recruited or locally differentiated cells displaying dysfunctional, regulatory, or IL-17-associated features that support myeloid cell recruitment, chronic inflammation, immune evasion, and therapy resistance. This review discusses the major recognition pathways, functional states, microbiota- and metabolite-dependent regulation, and therapeutic targeting of iNKT, MAIT, and γδ T cells in cancer. We further highlight emerging strategies to harness these cells through endogenous activation, combination immunotherapy, and engineered cell platforms while limiting tumor-promoting inflammatory programs and treatment-associated toxicity.
nc7a4bda7d381: Caspases are cysteine-aspartic proteases that mediate both lethal and non-lethal cellular outcomes, including the promotion of tissue growth. However, the mechanisms underlying the differential regulation of these activities remain unclear. We have previously shown that among the two Drosophila executioner caspases, Dcp-1 and Drice, Dcp-1 promotes tissue growth in a non-lethal manner, independent of canonical apoptotic signaling. Herein, we demonstrated that overexpressed Dcp-1, but not Drice, was activated without canonical apoptosome components. TurboID-based proximity labeling revealed distinct proximal proteomes, among which Sirtuin 1, an Atg8a deacetylase, which promotes autophagy, was specifically required for Dcp-1 activation. Autophagy-related genes, including Bcl-2 family members Debcl and Buffy, are required for Dcp-1 activation. Structure-based prediction using AlphaFold3 further identified Bruce, an autophagy-regulated inhibitor of apoptosis, as a Dcp-1-specific regulator acting outside the apoptosome-mediated pathway. Physiologically, Bruce suppresses wing tissue growth. These findings indicate that non-lethal Dcp-1 activity is governed by the autophagy–Bruce axis, enabling distinct non-lethal functions independent of cell death.
nc46288cc936d: Mutations in Syntaxin11 (STX11), a Q-SNARE, result in a fatal immune disorder known as familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis 4 (FHLH4) in human patients. A key diagnostic feature of FHLH4 is defective T and natural killer cell cytotoxicity. Here, we show that STX11 directly binds and regulates Orai1, the pore-forming subunit of calcium release-activated calcium (CRAC) channels. CRAC channels enable store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) from the extracellular space and are crucial for granule exocytosis and nuclear factor of activated T cells (NFAT)-dependent gene expression in activated lymphocytes. STX11 depletion strongly inhibited SOCE, CRAC currents, NFAT activation, interleukin-2 gene expression, and degranulation in FHLH4 patient T lymphocytes and cell lines without affecting membrane trafficking. Remarkably, defects of cytolytic granule exocytosis, as well as interleukin-2 expression, could be reversed by ionomycin in patient T lymphocytes, and a constitutively active, H134S, mutant of Orai1 rescued calcium entry in STX11-depleted cells. Further analyses showed that STX11 ‘primes’ Orai1 for optimal on-site multimeric assembly, which was Stim independent but required for gating. Priming of ion channel pore subunits is, therefore, a primary function of specific SNAREs which may have preceded their role in membrane trafficking and vesicle fusion.
nf40a30d8b8f9: The last 110 years have seen four influenza A pandemics, where viruses have emerged from mammals or birds with the ability to transmit and cause disease in human populations. Since 2021, a high-pathogenicity strain of avian influenza, H5N1, has caused a panzootic (pandemic of animals), with global spread in wild birds, resulting in frequent spillovers into farmed poultry and into mammals, including mammal species not previously known to be affected by influenza A. This has created increased opportunity for reassortment, mutation, human infection, and potential adaptation to transmit. The risk to humans and the impact are difficult to quantify but of mounting concern to public health bodies. Here, we examine the risk of an H5N1 pandemic emerging and spreading in humans and the potential impact of an H5N1 pandemic.
n1b8d5ef8fc0a: Passive anti–amyloid-β immunotherapy has shifted from repeated phase 3 failure to reproducible, although modest, clinical slowing in biomarker-defined early Alzheimer's disease. We review lessons from first-generation antibodies, including inadequate target engagement, late-stage enrollment, and limited outcome sensitivity. We then compare second-generation agents (i.e., aducanumab, lecanemab, and donanemab) highlighting amyloid-β species selectivity, plaque clearance kinetics, and durability, and we discuss emerging delivery innovations. Safety is dominated by amyloid-related imaging abnormalities, likely reflecting cerebrovascular amyloid vulnerability, and requires timely baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) screening; APOE -informed counseling; and standardized, front-loaded MRI surveillance with symptom-triggered evaluation. We summarize prevention trials in autosomal dominant and sporadic preclinical populations and consider prospects for combination or sequential regimens with tau-targeting therapies. Finally, we focus on biomarker-guided implementation: blood-based prescreening, confirmation pathways, monitoring of biological response, and treat-to-clear or stopping concepts, alongside unresolved issues of health-system readiness, equity, and budget impact. Registry-enabled learning is emphasized to generate real-world safety and effectiveness evidence.
n5d67d8c9fb69: Laboratory rats ( Rattus norvegicus ) have been invaluable to biomedical research and are well-suited for physiological analyses. Nevertheless, technical challenges in embryo and genetic manipulation have historically hindered the generation of genetically modified rats, thereby limiting their use for in vivo functional genetic studies. Recent advances, including genome editing and pluripotent/germline stem cell technologies, have substantially expanded rat genetic engineering. This review summarizes the historical background and recent advances in rat embryo manipulation and highlights the rapid development of genetic tools in rats, now catching up with those available in mice. These advances provide an opportunity to reassess the value of rats as experimental models. Furthermore, the combined use of mice and rats, exemplified by interspecific chimeras and comparative studies, offers new insights into conserved and species-specific physiological mechanisms across mammals.
n75b8f56767a0: Research on misinformation has expanded rapidly over the past decade. This review examines areas of consensus and contention within the literature on misinformation, with particular attention to conceptual definitions, measurement approaches, and theoretical explanations. We outline views on what it means to be susceptible to misinformation and advocate for assessing susceptibility by focusing on the ability to discern true from false claims. Although exposure to fake news is less common online than many think, we argue that misinformation—more broadly construed—continues to be a major problem. We review evidence on cognitive and socio-affective mechanisms underlying susceptibility to misinformation, including repetition effects, lack of analytic reasoning, political identity, and information environments. We also evaluate interventions such as fact-checking, prebunking, psychological inoculation, and accuracy prompts. Overall, the literature reveals several robust findings but also significant methodological limitations and theoretical disagreements that suggest fruitful future directions for misinformation research.
naa076d78042e: Ongoing liberalization and legalization of cannabis policy in the United States have shifted the focus of policy discussions to how legal markets should be regulated to protect public health. We reviewed the scientific literature on cannabis legalization, mapped current state cannabis policies using the National Conference of State Legislatures cannabis policy domains, and conducted a scoping review of peer-reviewed studies from 2015 to 2026 that measured specific cannabis policies and health or use outcomes. Across the 48 included studies, evidence was concentrated in licensing and business practices, nonmedical adult use regulations, medical program regulations, and local control. Our scoping review suggests that retail availability, outlet density, proximity, and local restrictions shape cannabis exposure and use. Evidence was limited for product regulations, taxes and revenue allocation, hemp/cannabidiol policies, justice system provisions, and public health/research policies. Future research should incorporate detailed policy coding, implementation measures, market data, surveillance data, and stronger researcher–policymaker linkages.

n40a110658caa: In situ glia-to-neuron conversion induced by a single transcription factor is a promising regenerative strategy for treating central nervous system injuries and neurodegenerative diseases. Previous studies reported that NeuroD1 can induce microglia-to-neuron cross-lineage conversion and improve recovery after brain injury. However, these findings remain controversial. To examine the ability of NeuroD1 in inducing microglia-to-neuron conversion, we employed virus-free genetic lineage-tracing systems in mice to specifically induce NeuroD1 expression in microglia and track the cell fate of NeuroD1-expressing cells at multiple timepoints. Meanwhile, we longitudinally monitored NeuroD1-expressing microglia via two-photon imaging and characterized their transcriptional profile by single-cell RNA sequencing. All observations across these methods revealed that NeuroD1-expressing cells retained their microglia identity and cannot convert into neurons, no matter under physiological and injury conditions. Instead, sustained expression of NeuroD1 facilitated microglia apoptosis in vivo. Collectively, our findings provide strong evidence that NeuroD1 alone is not sufficient to induce microglia-to-neuron conversion. This study further highlights the importance of rigorous lineage-tracing and cell fate-mapping strategies for validating in situ glia-to-neuron conversion.
n315bae484e0e: Two evolutionary highly conserved functions of dopamine are to carry ‘teaching’ signals during associative learning and to control movement. In mammals and humans, these functions are generally thought to be produced by different populations of neurons. Here, we investigated in the larva of Drosophila melanogaster whether both these functions can be induced by the same individual dopaminergic neurons in the central brain. Focusing on the dopaminergic neurons of the DL1 cluster, we asked whether the optogenetic activation of individual neurons established associative punishment and/or safety memories, controlled the retrieval of the established memories, and acutely modulated locomotion. We found that each neuron had a unique yet overlapping set of behavioural effects. Several individual neurons both established a memory and modulated acute locomotion by increasing the animals’ bending and decreasing their velocity. Our results demonstrate that individual dopaminergic neurons can fulfil a surprisingly broad range of functions in different behavioural contexts. Given the highly conserved roles of the dopaminergic system across the animal kingdom, this study raises the question whether a similarly diverse functionality can be found also in other animals, including humans.
nc5c6d2ad8737: The intestine integrates food-derived cues to coordinate organismal physiology, yet the molecular specialization of discrete regions along the intestinal epithelium remains unclear. Here, we generate cell type-specific translatomes of the Caenorhabditis elegans intestine during fasting and refeeding using discrete promoters for the anterior quartet of intestinal cells (INT1) and the remaining eight pairs of intestinal cells (INT2-9). We found that the anterior-most INT1 cells are a translationally distinct intestinal subcompartment that is particularly enriched for immune- and stress response genes. Functional assays using novel INT1-specific genes emerging from this study reveal that these specialized cells play a previously unappreciated role in pathogen avoidance and organismal survival. A second critical function of INT1 cells is their role in sensing and responding to the contents of the gut lumen. We show that luminal pyruvate is the key signal linking bacterial nutrients in the gut to secretion of the gut insulin antagonist INS-7. These findings establish INT1 as sentinel enteroendocrine cells that integrate metabolic and immune cues to couple food status with immune and endocrine responses. Our studies also provide a rich resource for dissecting segment-specific intestinal biology, an overlooked and fertile area for future research.
ne59939a9d42e: In many organisms, meiotic crossover recombination is suppressed near the extreme ends of chromosomes. Here, we show that multiple, often chromosome-specific, suppressive mechanisms with differing ranges contribute to the consistently low enrichment of recombination-promoting axis proteins and the downregulation of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) within 20 kb of telomeres in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Suppression of axis proteins is associated with cis-encoded signals and correlates with reduced coding density, although whether this sequence feature actively drives suppression remains to be determined. In addition, axis protein suppression requires the histone methyltransferase Dot1 and the Sir silencing complex. We show that Dot1 suppresses Sir complex activity at least in part independently of its canonical target, H3K79, to downmodulate axis protein deposition near chromosome ends. In parallel, the Sir complex, but not Dot1, suppresses the induction of DSBs at a small number of cryptic hotspots by limiting the openness of promoters, the preferred sites of meiotic DSB formation. Much of the reduced DSB induction near chromosome ends persists in dot1 and sir3 mutants, indicating that additional layers of regulation contribute to the robust reduction of meiotic recombination effectors near chromosome ends.
na73d950ebeae: Gross domestic product (GDP) remains the dominant measure of economic progress, despite long-standing critiques including its failure to account for environmental sustainability, inequality, and social well-being. In the context of escalating climate breakdown and rising inequality, GDP is increasingly being recognized as an inadequate metric for national prosperity. This article reviews the growing movement toward alternative measures that prioritize sustainability, inclusion, and the well-being of humans and the rest of nature. Hundreds of alternatives exist, but recent research shows significant similarity among them, forming the basis for building a broad consensus. This review explores how academics and policy makers are responding to the limitations of standard national accounts and highlights broad public support for expanding economic indicators. This review also identifies the key barriers to be overcome in order to move beyond GDP—including vested interests, institutional buy-in, and the fragmentation of alternatives—and suggests strategies to address each. By examining these barriers and evaluating potential solutions within the current political landscape, this review contributes to the discourse on how national accounting systems can better evolve to reflect the goals of a just and sustainable economy embedded in society and the rest of nature.
n742785456536: Cities are central to the climate challenge, but much research on urban climate action still focuses on emissions reductions within existing systems. This literature review assesses existing research and literature, including work on human-need-driven innovation for global sustainability and the export of globally sustainable solutions. Rather than limiting urban climate action to measures aimed at reaching zero emissions, the review examines an expanded urban innovation agenda in which cities are studied as incubators and exporters of innovations that support flourishing lives for all on a flourishing planet. The review synthesizes insights from sustainability transitions, sociotechnical systems, well-being economics, artificial intelligence, and brain science. Case studies from different cities illustrate how some urban innovation agendas are already shifting. The comparison highlights how a focus on flourishing lives can mobilize start-ups, youth, and public institutions, while addressing equity and positioning cities as actors in the next generation of urban climate action.
n3a7d451eec1f: Solar geoengineering is being suggested by some scientists as a partial solution to the climate crisis. However, these hypothetical technologies to reflect parts of incoming sunlight back out into space pose significant governance challenges, due to their ecological risks, planetary scale, and long-term consequences. This review examines the literature on solar geoengineering governance since 2020, identifying three strands of debate. The first explores emerging research governance and institutional arrangements for potential future deployment. The second, critical, strand focuses instead on institutional pathways to prohibit such technologies. A third strand analyzes the debate itself, including through the lens of science and technology studies. While proposals for solar geoengineering are developed by small groups of researchers in industrialized countries, opposition is growing in the Global South, with governments from Africa and the Pacific calling for an international nonuse agreement. This growing resistance from vulnerable nations raises pressing moral and political questions about continuing research amid mounting global dissent.
ne7ae710fe515: Groundwater, a crucial freshwater source worldwide, is under threat of salinization due to the combined pressures of climate change and human activities, hindering sustainable development. This review explores both natural and anthropogenic sources and mechanisms of groundwater salinization (GWS). We describe the impacts of GWS on environmental and socioeconomic systems, highlighting the risks to agriculture, water quality, and public health. We also discuss monitoring and assessment techniques and knowledge gaps essential for effective management. We present successful case studies of interventions in seven countries, showcasing the feasibility and difficulty of effective management and mitigation strategies. Finally, we address sustainability challenges and outline future directions for research and policy, emphasizing the need for a paradigm shift from reactive management to proactive, holistic, and adaptive stewardship.
n41ad8b772c19: This article introduces the metric selection framework (MSF), developed as part of the CVORR+ methodology. CVORR+ is a systems-based evaluation toolkit designed to support complex sustainability assessment and decision-making. Within CVORR+, the MSF translates system analysis into decision-oriented, multidimensional metrics for monitoring, assessment, and evaluation of progress toward sustainability targets. Grounded in a value-focused decision-making approach, the framework combines expert elicitation with stakeholder engagement to ensure that metrics are system grounded, context specific, and practically relevant. Applied to England's plastic packaging system, the MSF reveals systemic inefficiencies, identifies leverage points for intervention, and informs policy design to support systemic value recovery. The case study demonstrates the heuristic and practical value of the MSF in capturing interdependencies across environmental, economic, social, and technical domains. Future developments will streamline the translation from system conceptualization to metric development, ensuring that metrics are responsive to long-term monitoring and policy-making, remain aligned with technological and regulatory shifts, and enhance the robustness and transferability of CVORR+.
n019dd7f6eb81: Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) are an emerging area-based conservation mechanism aspiring to achieve long-term and effective in situ biodiversity conservation outside traditional protected areas. Contributing toward several global biodiversity targets, they combine protection with sustainable land use and human development. This review analyzes spatial and temporal trends in OECM site designation (2010–2024), exploring governance frameworks, management, and ecological effectiveness in reducing biodiversity loss, addressing environmental change, and promoting sustainable development. Emphasis is placed on inclusivity of OECMs, particularly engagement of local communities and Indigenous Peoples in stewardship and decision-making, thereby enhancing social equity and cultural relevance. Academic and policy attention has centered on two areas: ( a ) refining the OECM framework, its definition, characteristics, and alignment with international goals (Section 3), and ( b ) evaluating governance, effectiveness, and national/subnational implementation (Section 4). While OECMs offer potential to expand global conservation, issues around governance and site-level outcomes remain underexplored and warrant attention (Section 5).
n5cfcc1e81d61: Socioenvironmental research highlights the key role of communities and organizations in promoting sustainable and democratic energy systems. However, most of this emphasis has focused on modern industrialized societies. This article reviews research on energy alternatives conceptualized and practiced by movements and communities across the Global South. Based on the surveyed literature, we propose the concept of social energy futures (SEF) as an open-ended category to reflect on the drivers and features of these alternatives. As outlined, SEF are diverse and territorially situated, commonly encompassing three components: ( a ) they are largely needs-oriented, tending to prioritize use value over exchange value; ( b ) they involve broad political processes, defining how much energy should be harvested, through which technologies, by which actors, and for which purposes; and ( c ) they are part of broader identity struggles, reflecting how social actors actively organize to counteract colonial and corporate relations amid the energy and climate crisis. Taking these findings together, we propose an SEF analytical toolkit and outline future research themes to continue developing across diverse academic, cultural, and geographical settings.

n4cdfebedc395: The ability of humans to discriminate and identify spatial patterns varies across the visual field and is generally worse in the periphery than in the fovea. This decline in performance is revealed in many kinds of tasks, from detection to recognition. A parsimonious hypothesis is that the representation of any visual feature is blurred (spatially averaged) by an amount that differs for each feature, but that in all cases increases with eccentricity. Here, we examine models for two such features: local luminance and spectral energy. Each model averages the corresponding feature in pooling windows whose diameters scale linearly with eccentricity. We performed perceptual experiments with synthetic stimuli to determine the largest window scaling for which human and model discrimination abilities match (the ‘critical’ scaling). We used much larger stimuli than those of previous studies, subtending 53.6 by 42.2° of visual angle. We found that the critical scaling for the luminance model was approximately one-fourth that of the energy model and, consistent with earlier studies, that the estimated critical scaling value was smaller when discriminating a synthesized stimulus from a natural image than when discriminating two synthesized stimuli. Moreover, we found that initializing the generation of the synthesized images with natural images reduced the critical scaling value when discriminating two synthesized stimuli, but not when discriminating a synthesized from a natural image stimulus. Together, the results show that critical scaling is strongly affected by the image statistic (pooled luminance vs. spectral energy), the comparison type (synthesized vs. synthesized or synthesized vs. natural), and the initialization image for synthesis (white noise vs. natural image). We offer a coherent explanation for these results in terms of alignments and misalignments of the models with human perceptual representations.
