nac59e5d8be0d: In flowering plants, floral organ identity is specified by the combinatorial action of homeotic genes. While the role of these genes in the early specification of organ identity is well established, their late function throughout floral organ development and in specific cell types is much less characterized. In particular, since plant organs are structured in clonally independent cell layers, whether and how homeotic identity interacts with cell layer identity is unknown. We have previously identified cell layer-specific mutants for the petal identity gene PhDEF in petunia flowers, resulting in drastically different petal phenotypes whether PhDEF is expressed in the petal epidermis or in the mesophyll. In this study, using a combination of single-cell RNA-Seq and chromatin immunoprecipitation on phdef cell layer-specific mutants, we find that PhDEF regulates a different set of target genes in the petal epidermis and mesophyll, with a major regulatory action in the epidermis. We uncover a high diversity of binding profiles in PhDEF target genes, with a complex combination of layer-specific or non-specific binding sites, and a much more prominent binding of PhDEF in the epidermis than in the mesophyll. Our study highlights that floral homeotic genes like PhDEF can have different regulatory actions in different cell contexts, here different cell layers, demonstrating that cell layer identity indeed influences the regulatory processes underlying homeotic identity.
na0325eb023b8: Theropod dinosaur remains from the Barremian (Lower Cretaceous) Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, UK, are rare and often fragmentary. Here, we present a previously undescribed braincase from this formation that represents a new coelurosaurian, Invictibellatrix amberina gen. et sp. nov. Phylogenetic analysis and comparative anatomy indicate that Invictibellatrix is distantly related to all previously named theropods from this stratigraphic unit. Theropod braincases are often regarded as morphologically and phylogenetically conservative, but we demonstrate that neurocranial characters provide essential data that can help clarify the phylogenetic relationships of theropods. The sub-circular occipital condyle, sub-oval foramen magnum and presence of a sagittal nuchal crest indicate that Invictibellatrix is referable to Megaraptora, with phylogenetic analyses recovering it as an early-diverging member of this clade, within a paraphyletic array of Eurasian taxa. Incorporation of Invictibellatrix into a biogeographical analysis suggests that non-megaraptorid megaraptorans likely had a cosmopolitan distribution in the Early Cretaceous, and that the absence of megaraptorans in the Late Cretaceous of Laurasia is best explained by regional extinction. The recognition of this new genus increases our knowledge of Early Cretaceous European coelurosaurian diversity, which now includes tyrannosauroids, maniraptoriforms and megaraptorans.
n759fb0df395b: In past decades, conceptual analysis has established that evolution by natural selection (ENS) can occur without reproduction (Bouchard 2008 Philos. Sci. 75, 560–570 (doi:10.1086/594507); Papale, 2021 Synthese 198, 10 429–10 455 (doi:10.1007/s11229-020-02729-6)). The aim of this paper is to provide a computational proof of concept for this theoretical advance and to start assessing some of its conceptual upshots. To do so, we designed an agent-based model that introduces and defends a niche construction-based account of ENS without reproduction (ENSwR, pronounced like ‘answer’). Our results provide a computationally tractable proof of concept for ENSwR and a basis to reflect on some of its conceptual implications for debates regarding the origins of life. First, conceptual analysis suggests that ENSwR provides a novel explanatory framework that supports origins of life theories in which autocatalytic sets (ACSs) of chemical reactions play a central role (Xavier, Kauffman 2022 Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 380, 20210244 (doi:10.1098/rsta.2021.0244)). Second, through a discussion of the hydrothermal vent theory for the origins of life, we show that ENSwR will contribute to explaining the evolutionary origins of reproduction.
n9e969a1692e5: The herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) remains a relevant aquatic contaminant because parent-compound disappearance does not imply mineralization, detoxification or treatment readiness. This systematic review synthesizes recent evidence on advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) and closely related chemically coupled routes for aqueous 2,4-D treatment. Records from Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar within a documented 2020–2025 review window were screened using explicit eligibility criteria and assessed with an evidence-completeness rubric covering key reporting domains for cross-study comparison. The final corpus comprised 204 studies across photocatalytic/photo-assisted, electrochemical/electro-Fenton, Fenton-type, sulfate-radical, ozone-based, sonochemical, plasma-assisted and hybrid systems. Parent 2,4-D removal or analytical confirmation was reported in 202 studies, while carbon-based mineralization or organic-load evidence was reported in 116, transformation products in 95, residual toxicity in 27, real-water validation in 67 and reactor-scale or transferability information in 37. These patterns show stronger evidence for parent-compound disappearance than for treatment completeness, residual hazard and transferability. No AOP family was universally superior across removal, mineralization, toxicity reduction, matrix robustness, energy demand, durability and scale readiness. Future studies should standardize reporting of mineralization, transformation products, toxicity, energy boundaries, leaching, durability and reactor descriptors.
nfbe90dfa6f81: This study investigated the recovery and nanoliposomal formulation of anthocyanin-rich extracts from black rice using choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents (DESs). Choline chloride/1,2-propanediol (DES2) produced the highest anthocyanin content, 85.5 ± 3.4 mg l−1, after optimization, compared with 25.7 ± 2.1 mg l−1 obtained by conventional ethanol extraction. High-resolution QTOF-MS/MS enabled the tentative assignment of cyanidin 3-O-hexoside-type and peonidin 3-O-hexoside-type compounds based on accurate precursor masses and characteristic product ions; authentic-standard confirmation was not performed. The DES2 extract showed greater apparent thermal stability than the control extract, with estimated half-lives of 30.0 and 16.0 days, respectively, at 45°C. Anti-oxidant activity was observed in DPPH and ABTS assays, with IC50 values of 0.19 ± 0.06 and 0.16 ± 0.08 mg ml−1, respectively. Preliminary antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli was detected under the tested agar-diffusion conditions, whereas activity against Staphylococcus aureus was limited. Nanoliposomal encapsulation achieved an encapsulation efficiency of 73.8 ± 4.3%, a Z-average diameter of 201.3 nm and 89.83 ± 0.65% anthocyanin retention after 28 days at 4°C. The formulation produced a larger inhibition zone against E. coli than the free extract under the assay conditions. These findings support further investigation, although release kinetics, pharmaceutical efficacy and complete-process sustainability remain unestablished.
n58801560c7be: After the leakage of a buried pipeline, the overlying soil structure deforms under the high-speed impact of escaping gas, influencing both leakage and diffusion behaviours. This deformation typically appears as a soil cavity above the leakage port, especially in medium- and low-pressure conditions. In this study, the formation process of soil cavities is investigated using CFD–DEM coupled numerical simulations. The control variable method is applied to examine how different conditions affect cavity size and gas diffusion, and the sensitivity between cavity characteristics and leakage behaviour is analysed. Results show that the leaked gas forms a high-velocity zone near the leakage port, generating negative pressure in the surrounding area. Soil cavities generally form and stabilize within 0.1 s under gas impact. Soil particle size and porosity significantly influence the cavity formation time by altering the pore structure and total pore volume. The average sensitivity coefficients of the maximum cavity width to gas leakage velocity and the highest dangerous range (HDR) are 5.71 and 18.78, respectively, indicating that larger cavity widths correspond to higher leakage velocities and greater HDR. Therefore, the maximum cavity width serves as the most appropriate indicator for evaluating soil cavities caused by buried gas pipeline leakage.
n22e69b0de952: Urbanization poses a drastic threat to biodiversity, but does not affect all species equally. As such, identifying the life history traits and ecological characteristics that distinguish species that tolerate urban areas from those that do not is a central goal in urban ecology. Additionally, understanding whether shared evolutionary history influences urban tolerance could shed light on its evolutionary origins and reveal the extent to which urban landscapes filter out entire taxonomic clades, homogenizing biodiversity. Here, we assessed the relationship between urban tolerance and eight different life history and ecological traits for 431 North American bird species. We found that birds with higher urban tolerance are longer-lived, smaller-bodied, and more likely to be sedentary or mixed migrants than birds with lower urban tolerance. Birds with higher urban tolerance also have broader environmental tolerance, based on breeding range size and estimates of range-wide variation in precipitation, consistent with their greater likelihood of being habitat generalists. We additionally detected a phylogenetic signal for urban tolerance, with several clades sharing similar urban tolerance measures. Our study identifies several mechanisms that likely underlie species differences in urban tolerance and demonstrates how urban areas can filter bird species based on their life history and ecological traits.
n16111fed2f84: Many animals defend themselves with toxic chemicals and use multimodal warning displays involving odours and bright colours to advertise their toxicity. Yet, how coloration and odour interact and why they so often evolve together is not well understood. Recent work in jumping spiders has shown that defensive odours from three chemically defended bugs (Order Hemiptera: Acanthocephala femorata, Mormidea sp. and Leptoglossus phyllopus) increase a foraging aversion to red prey. Here, we ask whether these odours also increase avoidance of another visual warning: high-contrast stripes. Jumping spiders (Habronattus trimaculatus) were given choices between pattern-manipulated termites (solid white and black-and-white striped) in the presence or absence of a defensive odour from one of the aforementioned bug species. We predicted that any aversion to stripes would be stronger when odour was present. Surprisingly, we found no effect of any bug odour on the spiders’ aversions to stripes. Interestingly, these odours that so strongly and consistently trigger aversion to red do not have the same effect on stripes. This highlights the different ways that odours and coloration can interact (or not) to influence predators, providing insight into the diversity of aposematic displays in nature.
n74f0a6ed12d1: Parent–offspring communication depends on offspring signals that help parents assess need and allocate care. Nestling begging is often treated as a graded, information-rich and therefore honest signal of hunger, as predicted by costly signalling models. We quantified how effectively visual and acoustic begging components encode food deprivation in spotless starling (Sturnus unicolor) nestlings using field observations and a controlled laboratory experiment. We combined random-regression models with information-theoretic measures of uncertainty reduction and receiver-based machine-learning decoding. In wild broods, begging order and maximum postural intensity increased with deprivation time, yet posture and calling together reduced uncertainty about deprivation by less than 5%. Distinct postural levels overlapped widely among deprivation states and followed a stereotyped sequence—rapid escalation to maximum intensity followed by relaxation—yielding poor resolution of intermediate hunger. Adding components improved decoding only marginally beyond the first few cues. Parental allocation was correspondingly rapid, although display duration could provide additional information once the full bout was perceived. Discrete coding analyses confirmed that simple postural schemes were most consistent and that begging reliably distinguished only coarse, extreme hunger states. Overall, the results support partially informative (pooling) or attention-seeking signalling models in which parents rely on a small set of salient cues within a multi-component display.
n98b2558dccf9: Social isolation measures enforced during the COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of the social environment in shaping affective states and decision-making. However, the day-to-day experience and psychological recovery from social deprivation, especially among individuals with high trait anxiety, remains poorly understood. We conducted a 10-day longitudinal study with 116 university students returning to campus, collecting approximately 31 000 momentary assessments of affect and social interactions during a 3-day quarantine and subsequent period. Quarantine increased the need for social interaction and altered patterns of social engagement, whereas trait anxiety was robustly associated with reduced positive affect and elevated negative affect. Close interactions following quarantine were associated with higher positive affect. We also administered a virtual patch-foraging task to participants during and after quarantine. Greater variability in negative affect was associated with lower patch exit thresholds, suggesting a tendency to persist in depleted patches. These findings highlight how trait anxiety shapes emotional experience and social behaviour in daily life and reveal how fluctuations in negative affect can influence sequential decision-making under uncertainty.
n4b076bcf5895: Changes in the axial skeleton played an important role in dinosaur evolution, with some of the oldest dinosaurs showing evidence of sacralization events. The increased number of early dinosaur discoveries over the last decade provides an opportunity to better characterize this phenomenon. It has led us to revise our understanding of axial evolution in early dinosaurs. Results support that the last common ancestor of Dinosauria would probably present 9 cervical, 16 dorsal and 2 sacral vertebrae (primordials). Early saurischians maintain a consistent number of vertebrae with presacral origin, and there is no evidence of meristic changes in these dinosaurs. A more complex scenario is observed in early ornithischians (including ‘silesaurids’). An insertion between the primordials occurs early in ornithischian evolution, and it appears to be maintained in ‘traditional’ ornithischians (Saphornithischia). Unambiguous evidence supports loss and gain of presacral vertebrae in ornithischians. Inserted sacrals across all dinosaurs are associated with a loss of a corresponding dorsal vertebra, supporting that these represent trunk vertebrae moved into the sacrum rather than novel vertebral unities. Changes in the axial skeleton of early dinosaurs are dominated by homeotic processes, with meristic processes restricted to derived members.
n48ca4bc88a65: The material properties of bone in the skull are known to be heterogeneous and orthotropic, although datasets detailing these properties on a species level are limited. Therefore, computational modelling frequently uses homogeneous, isotropic material properties to analyse stresses/strains in the skull. However, it is often unknown how the choice of bone/s from which the elastic modulus is measured, or the direction in which it is measured, influences predicted stresses/strains. This study integrated imaging and measured muscle properties to create a subject-specific finite element model of a rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus) skull, to investigate the influence of modelling the elastic modulus of bone through varying levels of complexity. The results demonstrate the importance of modelling orthotropic material properties, if known. Strain distribution was insensitive to whether the same isotropic elastic modulus was used for all bones in the skull versus modelling bone-specific isotropic elastic modulus. Strain distribution was also similar when using an isotropic elastic modulus based on measurement in different orthotropic directions, albeit with a slight difference when measured in the medio-lateral direction. This highlights that isotropic, homogeneous modelling of the skull is appropriate when analysing strain distribution, although alternative material modelling should be considered when strain magnitude is of particular interest.
ndacf7e2b40da: Groundwater-dependent ecosystems are biodiversity hotspots that provide habitat for specialized species. The European Union (EU) Water Framework Directive (WFD) stresses the importance of identifying and protecting these ecosystems. So far, most studies focus on (semi-) arid regions, where groundwater use by ecosystems is both more prevalent and easier to detect. In this study, we adapt groundwater-dependent vegetation (GDV) mapping approaches developed for dry climates to temperate regions by replacing seasonal drought-based indicators with contrasts between dry and wet years. We implement this concept by integrating for the first time to our knowledge, ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration data with high-resolution remote sensing, regional geospatial data and botanical field observations. To test our framework, we trained and validated random forest models with eight predictor variables using 166 vegetation plots to identify GDV in Central Germany. Ground-truth GDV plots prefer cooler, wetter, nutrient-richer and more acidic to alkaline environments compared to non-GDV. The final model using a phreatophyte cover threshold of 25% representing GDV plots achieved a testing accuracy of 0.97, identifying 2067 km² of GDV. Currently, only 19% is protected under the EU WFD. The proposed mapping framework offers a solution for identifying GDV in temperate regions. The new GDV maps can contribute to managing groundwater resources and preserving biodiversity hotspots in regions facing increasing droughts, ultimately supporting the implementation of the EU WFD.
n757380213509: Climatic variation can shape primate activity budgets by altering the energetic and thermoregulatory costs of feeding, resting, locomotion and social behaviour. However, little is known about how chimpanzees that inhabit cool, wet montane forests adjust their activity in response to fine-scale meteorological conditions. We examined the effects of temperature, absolute humidity (water vapour pressure (WVP)), wind speed and rainfall on eastern chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes schweinfurthii) in Nyungwe National Park, Rwanda, one of the highest-elevation chimpanzee habitats. From March 2024 to February 2025, we collected 1933 party scans and 5661 individual scans, together with scan-level microclimatic measurements. Rainfall showed the clearest behavioural association: feeding probability declined during rainfall, whereas resting increased. Wind speed was negatively associated with both locomotion and grooming, suggesting that windier conditions may constrain movement and social behaviour. Temperature, WVP and fruit availability showed no clear association with any of the four behaviours. Feeding probability was higher and resting probability lower in the wet season than in the dry season. Harmonic beta-binomial generalized linear mixed-effects models revealed pronounced daily rhythmicity in feeding and resting. Overall, Nyungwe chimpanzees maintained broadly conserved daily activity rhythms while selectively adjusting behavioural allocation in response to immediate meteorological conditions.
na44cd5eb6c38: Development of sustainable hydrogen production methods is crucial for the future hydrogen economy. Hence, designing cheap, stable and efficient catalysts for hydrogen generation is important. Here, we present the use of the family of eight Schiff base ligand-based transition metal complexes [MnIII(Salen)Cl] 1/[CoII(Salen)], 2/[NiII(Salen)], 3/[CuII(Salen)], 4/[MnIII(CH3Salen)Cl], 5/[CoII(CH3Salen)], 6/[NiII(CH3Salen)], 7/[CuII(CH3Salen)] and 8 (Salen/N,N′-bis(salicylidene)ethylenediamine/H2L1; CH3Salen/N,N′-bis(o-hydroxyacetophenone)ethylenediamine/H2L2) as hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts. Electrochemical studies for the complexes (in CH3CN) were carried out in the absence and presence of acids. Catalytic parameters of turnover frequency/overpotential were calculated for the electrocatalytic process. All complexes were found to be efficient HER catalysts in the presence of acids and Co/Ni/Cu complexes were more stable than the Mn complexes. The stability and efficiency order of the catalysts was 2, 4 > 6 > 7 > 3 > 8 (acetic acid); 1 > 5 (trifluoroacetic acid). Density functional theory studies provided detailed insight into the metal- versus ligand-centred redox transitions and the HER mechanism for all complexes. Successive events of electrochemical reduction (E) and protonation (C) along the HER paths were investigated, and thermodynamically feasible routes were assigned. This work provides insights into the effect of a series of earth-abundant transition metal complex structures, the performance of this series of metal centres on electrocatalysis, and the effect of pKa on reactivity. Hence, it will be of value to develop novel and promising catalysts for HER in the future.
nb699c2f6b386: Aggressive and affiliative interactions shape resource allocation, social structure and reproduction in social species. In delphinids, rake marks (parallel scars from tooth raking) indicate social interactions. When examined alongside ontogeny, demographic traits and scar position, rake marks can inform social dynamics. We assessed rake marks on common dolphins (Delphinus delphis) in Aotearoa New Zealand (2006–2024; n = 102) during post-mortem examinations to explore drivers of social behaviour. Using a zero-inflated generalized linear mixed model, we assessed rake mark occurrence (probability of rake density > 0) and prevalence (rake density, rake marks dm−2) across the body (n = 101; dorsal/ventral, cranial/caudal, left/right) in relation to sex, age, total body length (TBL), sexual maturity, body condition (n = 101) and female reproductive status (n = 51), to infer confrontation, avoidance and lateralization. Females showed higher rake mark prevalence but lower occurrence than males, suggesting infrequent but prolonged interactions, possibly sexual coercion. Rake prevalence and occurrence increased with TBL, potentially related to increased social interactions and surface area in larger individuals. Age, sexual maturity, body condition, and female reproductive status were not strong predictors of rake mark occurrence or prevalence. Our findings highlight rake marks as potential indicators of social dynamics.
n2165ce6e22a8: Polyethylene (PE) is a highly recalcitrant polymer that resists microbial degradation owing to its hydrophobic and chemically inert structure. In this study, a Streptomyces sp. strain MH-1, isolated from the earthworm gut, was investigated for its interaction with PE under carbon-limited conditions. The strain was associated with approximately 15% reduction in PE weight after 30 days of incubation. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) analysis revealed alterations in polymer chemistry, including a reduction in the carbonyl peak (approx. 1715 cm‒1) and a decrease in the carbonyl index from 0.19 in the control to 0.10 in treated samples. In silico analysis using a closely related Streptomyces genome as a reference framework identified putative genes associated with hydrocarbon metabolism and suggested potential oxidative and assimilatory pathways. Candidate aldehyde dehydrogenases, including bifunctional alcohol/aldehyde dehydrogenase (adhE), together with genes associated with fatty acid metabolism and β-oxidation, may indicate potential mechanisms involved in the processing of oxidation intermediates. These findings, combined with biofilm formation and growth under confined conditions, highlight the importance of PE-associated microenvironments and provide a basis for exploring microbial adaptation and potential metabolic processes involved in PE biotransformation.
n83cd880dfd35: Most fish species are ectothermic and rely on behavioral strategies to control their body temperature in heterothermal environments. Both thermotaxis and thermokinesis have been suggested as important underlying mechanisms. However, to what extent these behaviors allow fish to respond to rapid (timescales of minutes) and strong thermal disturbances, like those caused by anthropogenic water releases into natural freshwater systems, is poorly understood. Here, we quantify this response for a salmonid species with a novel laboratory approach coupled with image-based tracking. We exposed brown trout parr (Salmo trutta), acclimated to 12 °C, to rapidly forming cold- and warm-water interfaces with temperatures ranging from 4 to 20 °C. We found that fish actively avoided colder water (≤8 °C) through a rapid response that combined thermotaxis and thermokinesis. In contrast, fish did not avoid warmer water and frequently crossed interfaces having temperature contrasts of up to 8 °C. This study shows that brown trout parr swiftly deploy multiple behavioral strategies to minimize exposure to cold water and take advantage of warm water, illustrating their capability to cope with rapidly occurring thermal alterations.
n9f3420dadd55: Large language models are very good at providing concise answers. But if we only see the answer without knowing the original question or the context behind it, that answer may not be very useful. The important issue is not simply how much information an AI summary removes but whether we can still recover the missing context. Thus, AI literature tools should also report how much information was removed and how recoverable their omissions are.
nef412af17fca: Neurons represent changes in external and internal environments by altering their activity patterns. While coherent brain-wide patterns of neural activity have been observed in neuronal populations, very little is known about their dimensionality, geometry, and how they are correlated with sensory inputs. Here, we recorded the activity of most head neurons in Caenorhabditis elegans experiencing changes in bacterial or control buffer stimuli around their nose. We first classified active neurons into six functional clusters: two sensory neuron clusters (ON and OFF responding to addition and removal of stimuli, respectively) and four motor/command neuron clusters (AVA, RME, SMDD, and SMDV). Next, we estimated stimulus selectivity for each cluster and found that while sensory neurons exhibit their maximal responses within 15 s, changes in bacterial stimuli drive maximal responses in command and motor neuron clusters after tens of seconds. Furthermore, we show that bacterial stimuli induce neural dynamics that are best described by a hyperbolic, not Euclidean, space indicating hierarchical organization in C. elegans neural population dynamics. This space was 8-dimensional, with dimensions that aligned in one sensory direction (ON and OFF neurons), two motor directions (forward-backward and dorsal-ventral), and the rest of dimensions corresponding with unclassified neurons. Collectively, we show that C. elegans neural activity can be effectively represented in low-dimensional hyperbolic space and describe how sensory information is processed by the neural network.
n7d6adc2ffcb6: Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA)-G is selectively expressed by fetal trophoblast cells that encounter maternal natural killer (NK) cells early in pregnancy. In response to HLA-G, the endosomal NK cell receptor KIR2DL4 induces a transcriptional program to support placental development. Structural features of KIR2DL4 that control HLA-G binding and endocytosis are unclear. Random mutagenesis revealed that three cysteines in the first immunoglobulin domain of KIR2DL4 regulate endocytosis and uptake of HLA-G. The atypical Cys10–Cys28 disulfide bond in the KIR2DL4 structure is an allosteric disulfide with potential to switch to a conventional Cys28–Cys74 bond. KIR2DL4 in human cells exists in both disulfide-bonded states, as shown by mass spectrometry analysis. The Cys10–Cys28 bond in a Cys74Ser KIR2DL4 mutant was reduced by protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) in vitro. Inhibition of PDI prevented HLA-G uptake by KIR2DL4 in NK cells. Mutants in the Cys10–Cys28 configuration endocytosed spontaneously but did not bind HLA-G. Conversely, KIR2DL4 with a Cys28–Cys74 bond was detectable at the plasma membrane and internalized soluble HLA-G. A purified Cys10Leu KIR2DL4 mutant bound HLA-G with micromolar affinity in a peptide-dependent manner. Thus, allosteric disulfide-mediated conversion from an inactive to an HLA-G binding form regulates KIR2DL4 trafficking and a functional response that promotes fetal development.
n8eab5f59da73: Human African trypanosomiasis (HAT) is a neglected tropical disease transmitted by infected tsetse flies (Glossina spp.) in sub-Saharan Africa. Infected tsetse flies can transmit trypanosomes, including Trypanosoma brucei subspecies that cause HAT in humans, as well as other trypanosome species that cause animal African trypanosomiasis in domestic animals and infect wildlife. Tsetse flies feed on a broad spectrum of hosts, including humans, elephants, buffaloes, rhinos, hippos, turtles, and monitor lizards. To understand how the insects can penetrate such diverse skin types, we detailed the anatomical structures involved in tsetse blood feeding, their mechanical properties, and the forces exerted by the fly during probing. We found that the tsetse fly’s feeding apparatus does not rely on exceptionally unique structures or extraordinary forces. Instead, the tsetse fly has evolved subtle yet highly efficient adaptations, which include a labellum equipped with arrays of small teeth. When combined with a robust retraction movement of the proboscis, these structures create lesions on various types of skin, thus facilitating blood pool feeding on a broad host spectrum.
n064370a640bf: Investigating the dynamics of neural networks, which are governed by connectivity between neurons, is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Because passive (spontaneous) activity provides only limited information for estimating connectivity, perturbation-based approaches are widely applied in neuroscience as they can evoke underlying hidden dynamics. However, the characteristics of such perturbations have typically been designed based on empirical or biological intuition. To enable more accurate estimation of connectivity, we propose a data-driven and theoretically grounded framework for optimally designing perturbation inputs, based on formulating the neural model as a control system. The core theoretical insight underlying our approach is that neural signals observed in the passive state lack sufficient latent information, which leads to failures in the system identification. Perturbations reveal these hidden dynamics and lead to improved estimation. Guided by these insights, we derive a theoretical basis for optimizing perturbation inputs that minimize estimation errors in neural system identification. Building upon this, we further explore the relationship of this theory with stimulation patterns commonly used in neuroscience, such as frequency, impulse, and step inputs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework for neuroscience through simulations grounded in experimental paradigms, such as neural state classification and optimal control of neural states. Our theoretical analysis, together with multiple simulations, consistently shows that perturbations designed according to our framework achieve substantially more accurate system identification compared to the conventional, intuition-based inputs. This study provides a theoretical foundation for designing perturbation inputs to achieve accurate estimation of neural dynamics. This, in turn, enables reliable discrimination of neural states such as levels of consciousness and pathological conditions, and facilitates precise control of their transitions toward recovery from abnormal states.
n8c5e9d26a1ec: Neural circuit assembly relies on the precise regulation of cell-surface receptors that mediate signaling and adhesion. Endocytosis controls receptor activity and availability by internalizing and routing proteins through early endosomes to one of two main pathways: recycling back to the cell-surface or delivery to lysosomes for degradation. Rab GTPases direct receptors into these distinct pathways, but their specific contributions to circuit formation remain opaque. Using clonal analyses with null alleles, we dissected the roles of Rab-mediated trafficking to early, late, and recycling endosomes across multiple stages of circuit assembly in vivo. Our approach revealed that Rab5 and Rab11 regulate extensive and largely distinct developmental events, highlighting the pivotal roles of early endosome sorting and recycling pathways in circuit assembly. As neurons mature, both the spatial distribution and abundance of specific endocytic compartments change to reflect evolving trafficking demands. Our findings underscore how distinct post-endocytic trafficking fates are necessary to build neural circuits.
n26830a9e154a: Glycogen phosphorylase (GP) catalyzes the rate-limiting step of glycogenolysis and supplies precursors for chitin biosynthesis in insects. Acyl urea compounds structurally related to benzoylphenylurea (BPU) insecticides are potent inhibitors of mammalian GP, raising the question of whether insect GP could serve as an independent insecticidal target. Here, we show that a mammalian GP inhibitor (GPI) potently inhibits recombinant Plutella xylostella GP (PxGP; IC50=2.96 nM), while the BPU insecticide diflubenzuron does not. Molecular docking and MM/GBSA analysis predict that this selectivity reflects differential side-chain engagement. Despite potent in vitro inhibition, GPI exhibits no insecticidal activity, and RNAi-mediated knockdown of PxGP does not impair development or survival. We provide evidence that insects compensate through upregulation of gluconeogenic enzymes (PEPCK, G-6-Pase) and protein catabolism, with enzyme activity measurements confirming ~29% reduction in GP-a activity following RNAi. Fitness assessment reveals transient larval weight loss with complete recovery of pupal weight, adult morphology, and fecundity. These findings demonstrate that GP is functionally non-essential under the tested conditions, likely through gluconeogenic compensation and alternative carbon sources, and highlight the importance of metabolic network redundancy in target-based insecticide design.
